dz.headline: Algerian police recover 23 billion centimes from criminal network
dz.dek: Authorities arrested 25 individuals involved in counterfeiting, fraud, and money laundering across multiple regions.
paragraphs: Algerian police dismantled a criminal network involved in counterfeiting, fraud, and money laundering on October 29. The operation, led by the central service for combating organized crime, recovered 23 billion centimes from the group's illicit activities. The network operated across several regions of Algeria.

The Directorate General of National Security (DGSN) reported that the criminals used over 400 fictitious business registrations for fraudulent transactions to move money outside legal channels. This activity caused an estimated loss of 9200 billion centimes to the public treasury. Police seized trucks, cars, seals, and administrative documents during the operation.

25 members of the network were arrested and presented to the national economic and financial crimes division. Investigations supervised by the competent prosecutor's office revealed the methods used to deceive control services.

dz.headline: Algeria seizes 2.4 million psychotropic pills
dz.dek: 10 suspects arrested and charged with drug trafficking in Algiers
paragraphs: Algerian authorities seized 2.4 million psychotropic pills in a major operation against drug trafficking networks. 10 individuals were arrested on Thursday and placed under detention orders by an investigating judge at the Sidi M’hamed tribunal.

The suspects, identified by the prosecution as Rachid Merabet, 44, Hocine Touil, 37, Nabil Ghazal, 32, Fouad Ghazal, 29, Nassim Touil, 39, Ahamed Benaziza, 37, Akram Benaziza, 26, Oussama Tifoura, 31, Ziad Asnine, 23, and Idriss Gharbi, 44, were caught in possession of the Pregabalin 300 mg tablets. The prosecution also stated that the identities of five other individuals who are currently fugitives have been established.

The operation targeted networks involved in the trafficking of these psychotropic substances. The judge ordered the detention of the 10 suspects on charges related to organized crime and transnational terrorism.

dz.headline: Algerian businesses explore trade opportunities in China
dz.dek: Linyi city hosts international buyers conference to foster economic and investment cooperation.
paragraphs: Algerian businesses are exploring new avenues for trade and partnership at the fourth International Buyers Conference in Linyi, China. The event, running from October 28-30, aims to boost commercial exchange and economic cooperation, aligning with the Belt and Road Initiative. Officials and business representatives from China and other nations are attending to discover commercial, industrial, and logistical potentials.

The conference provides a platform to expand international partnerships and develop cross-border e-commerce, connecting global markets with Chinese production centers. Yu Shengtao, Deputy Secretary of the CPC Linyi Municipal Committee and Mayor, highlighted the city's historical legacy, economic capacity, and integrated logistics services as key strengths for wholesale trade and distribution. He encouraged foreign investors to leverage these opportunities for mutual benefit.

Chen Baiwei, Director-General of the Foreign Affairs Office of the CPC Shandong Provincial Committee, noted that previous conferences have successfully fostered economic and trade exchanges, attracting international buyers. He expressed hope that this event will lead to new partnerships between Chinese and foreign businesspeople, supporting international trade development and economic communication.

dz.headline: Algeria launches major non-hydrocarbon export drive
dz.dek: The operation on November 7 will see companies like Condor and Faderco ship goods to multiple countries.
paragraphs: Algeria is preparing an unprecedented export operation for non-hydrocarbon products, involving companies from various regions. Coordinated by the Ministry of the Interior, the initiative aims to boost non-oil and gas exports and showcase national industrial and artisanal potential. The operation is scheduled for Saturday, November 7.

Several companies are participating, including Condor, Iris, and Faderco. Condor, an appliance giant, will send 400 containers of household goods and metal structures to Tunisia, Egypt, Jordan, Libya, and Mauritania. Faderco, a hygiene product leader, plans to export 50 containers of hygiene items and raw materials to the United States, the United Kingdom, Tunisia, and Ivory Coast.

This event follows a similar export drive on April 11 that reached 19 countries. Algeria exported $4 billion in non-hydrocarbon products in the first eight months of 2026 and aims for $5 billion by year-end. Companies from 13 wilayas, including Bordj Bou Arreridj and Algiers, are involved.

dz.headline: Algeria identifies 362 sites for tourism investment
dz.dek: Minister Houria Messaoudi announced the availability of land parcels across 26 provinces to boost the hospitality sector.
paragraphs: Algerian Minister of Tourism and Handicrafts, Houria Messaoudi, has identified 362 real estate plots suitable for tourism investment across 26 provinces. The minister chaired a coordination meeting to assess the status of tourism real estate and track efforts to inventory available plots for investors via the Algerian Agency for Investment Promotion's platform.

Messaoudi stated that developing domestic and Saharan tourism depends on providing prepared, exploitable land parcels free from technical and administrative obstacles. During the meeting, it was revealed that 150 of these plots are currently being developed within sectoral programs for tourism expansion zones.

The meeting also reviewed 240 plots made available to the Algerian Agency for Investment Promotion across 30 tourism expansion zones, with 31 land shares already granted to investors. Efforts are underway to demarcate these zones to protect them from encroachment and update land data in coordination with state property services and local authorities.

ao.headline: Kiluanji Kia Henda film premieres at Rotterdam festival
ao.dek: The Angolan artist's new film, "Karl Marx, Luanda," combines African science fiction with spaghetti westerns.
paragraphs: Angolan artist Kiluanji Kia Henda's new film, "Karl Marx, Luanda," will premiere at the 56th Rotterdam Film Festival from January 28 to February 7, 2027. The film imagines Angola renewing its commitment to communism and tells a love story with time travel. It blends African science fiction with spaghetti western elements, as described by the festival.

The movie is a co-production between Angola and Portugal, with Wonder Maria Filmes involved. This marks Henda's return to the Rotterdam festival, where he previously presented a performance in 2021. Henda, born in 1979, is a multidisciplinary artist who explores collective memory, public spaces, and society, often reflecting on post-colonialism.

Henda received Angola's National Prize for Art and Culture in 2012 and the Frieze Artist Award in 2017. His work has been exhibited internationally, including at the Centre George Pompidou in Paris, Tate Modern in London, and the Guggenheim in Bilbao. He is also creating a Memorial to Enslaved People for Lisbon.

ao.headline: Angolan opposition forms civic monitoring platform
ao.dek: Four political parties and two civil society groups created a platform to ensure electoral integrity for 2027.
paragraphs: Four Angolan political parties, Bloco Democrático (BD), PDP-ANA, PNSA, and PPA, have joined forces with the Angolan Federation of Associations of People with Disabilities (FAPED) and the MUDEI movement to establish a Joint Civic Monitoring Platform.

This platform emerged from a National Conference on the Electoral Process (CNPE 2026) held in Luanda, which gathered over 300 representatives from civil society, youth, and human rights groups in late September to propose solutions for electoral integrity.

The group aims to create specific legislation defining electoral red lines and will demand strict adherence from the National Electoral Commission (CNE) and the Ministry of Territorial Administration (MAT) regarding vote counting, data integrity, and voter registration accessibility.

ao.headline: Angola's MPLA summons general Higino Carneiro for disciplinary hearing
ao.dek: The ruling party's Central Committee will investigate alleged document forgery and ethical breaches by the general.
paragraphs: Angolan general Higino Carneiro was summoned on Thursday, October 29, 2026, to appear before the MPLA's Central Committee Discipline and Audit Commission on Friday at 9:00 AM. This summons follows the committee's October 21 decision to nullify Carneiro's candidacy for party leadership and initiate disciplinary proceedings against him.

Carneiro had intended to challenge current MPLA president and President of the Republic, João Lourenço, at the party's IX Congress on December 9-10. His candidacy, submitted on June 25, was initially rejected due to alleged "grave irregularities," including falsified signatures and misuse of identification documents, according to MPLA official Job Capapinha.

The MPLA's Political Bureau upheld the rejection, forwarding the case to the Central Committee, which confirmed the nullification and decided to inform the Attorney General's Office due to strong indications of document forgery. The committee cited Carneiro's "voluntary and conscious violation of ethical and moral duties" as grounds for the disciplinary action.

ao.headline: Angola uses penal code against journalists
ao.dek: The constitution guarantees free expression, but courts prosecute reporters for defamation.
paragraphs: Angolan authorities are systematically using the Penal Code to prosecute journalists, despite the Constitution guaranteeing freedom of expression and the press. This practice violates international commitments made by the state, according to Folha 8.

Journalists in Angola who report on corruption, nepotism, or abuses of power often face criminal charges such as insult, slander, or defamation. These accusations are used by political figures and groups to silence critical reporting and investigative journalism.

This approach criminalizes speech and inverts the basic logic of democracy, where public scrutiny is a duty of the press and a right of citizens. The persistent use of the courts under the guise of protecting 'honor' neutralizes investigative journalism and critical voices.

bj.headline: Benin president attends AICESIS board meeting in Madrid
bj.dek: Abdoulaye Bio Tchané participated in discussions on climate change, technological transformations, and social dialogue.
paragraphs: Abdoulaye Bio Tchané, president of Benin's Economic and Social Council (CES), attended an AICESIS board meeting in Madrid, Spain, on October 29 and 30, 2026. The meeting reviewed the 2025 activity report and outcomes from international forums held in China, Russia, and Zimbabwe. Discussions also covered the organization's financial situation, noting a surplus in treasury despite a budgetary deficit.

The AICESIS board examined reports on international forums focusing on climate change, technological transformations, and social dialogue. Benin's CES president, Abdoulaye Bio Tchané, participated for the first time as a new board member. The meeting also addressed the interest of several councils in joining AICESIS and welcomed new officials from member councils, including Greece.

The participation of Benin's CES aims to strengthen cooperation with peer institutions and contribute to international exchanges on economic and social issues. The discussions provided opportunities for experience sharing and consolidating relationships between represented institutions. Benin's CES reaffirmed its commitment to dialogue and international cooperation for equitable development.

bj.dek: The cotonou stage of the benin beach tour concluded on october 25, 2026, with Akpakpa Boys and Ace claiming the men's and women's titles respectively.
paragraphs: Akpakpa Boys and Ace were crowned champions of the cotonou stage of the Bénin Beach Tour on Sunday, October 25, 2026, at Erevan beach. The event, which ran from October 23 to 25, showcased the skill and endurance of beninese beach-volleyball players.

Organized by the Fédération béninoise de volleyball (Fbvb) under the supervision of Colonel Oscar Dafia, the tour aims to develop beach-volleyball in Benin. The next stage will be held in Parakou in December 2026.

bj.headline: Beninese student wins fourth global UPU prize
bj.dek: Marie-Ange Chekpo, 15, also took first national prize for her letter on digital age relationships.
paragraphs: 15-year-old Marie-Ange Chekpo from Godomey won the fourth global prize in the 55th Universal Postal Union (UPU) international letter-writing competition. She received her award on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, in Cotonou, after also securing the national first prize and an international jury special mention.

Chekpo, a student at Le Bon Berger school in Godomey, wrote about why human relationships remain important in an increasingly digital world. Benin ranked behind China, Portugal, and Iran in this year's competition, which saw 1.48 million participants from 65 countries.

The UPU competition, established in 1971, is open to young people aged 9 to 15. For the 2026 edition, the UPU partnered with the World Health Organization and UNESCO to focus on human connections in the digital era.

bj.headline: Benin sextortion victims fear judgment
bj.dek: Women and girls make up 69% of sextortion victims in Benin, facing shame and fear of exposure.
paragraphs: Sextortion, where intimate images are used for blackmail, is a hidden crime in Benin. Victims like Houéfa, who was threatened with shared videos in 2016, suffer in silence due to fear of judgment and lack of knowledge about available help. Organizations are now working on prevention and support for those affected by this digital violence.

The Centre national d’investigations numériques (CNIN) reported that 69% of sextortion victims in Benin are women and girls, according to Matin Libre on February 20, 2026. Sociologist Dr. MONTCHO Bruno emphasizes that prevention campaigns must address the social, economic, and digital realities of victims to combat the shame and vulnerability that prevent them from seeking assistance.

bw.headline: Botswana launches P1 billion fund for industry
bw.dek: The Diamonds for Development Fund aims to convert mineral wealth into sustainable enterprises and jobs.
paragraphs: Botswana has launched its P1 billion Diamonds for Development Fund to create industries and jobs, moving beyond its reliance on diamond revenue. The fund received its initial P1 billion from De Beers Group. This initiative aims to transform wealth from the country's soil into diversified resources that generate value long after diamonds are depleted.

Established through a partnership between the Government of Botswana and De Beers Group, the fund intends to attract investment, nurture businesses, and expand the nation's export base. Chairman Dr. Akinwumi A. Adesina stated that the fund will convene government, business, and financial institutions to develop high-potential opportunities into investable projects.

The fund's strategy is to act as a catalyst, de-risking and packaging opportunities to attract private capital. This approach addresses the common challenge in Africa where promising ventures fail to become viable projects due to a lack of structure or funding.

bw.headline: Botswana secures $503.75 million loan from AfDB
bw.dek: The new financing offers budget relief but raises questions about future revenue and debt repayment.
paragraphs: Botswana has secured a US$503.75 million loan, equivalent to P6.62 billion, from the African Development Bank (AfDB) approved last Friday, October 23. This new facility provides financial relief and is roughly a quarter of the P26.35 billion deficit projected for the 2026/27 financial year.

The latest loan follows a US$304 million facility approved on May 14, 2025, for the 2025/26 fiscal year, which was fully disbursed by June 2026. Finance Minister Ndaba Gaolathe had previously outlined a five-year grace period followed by 15 years of repayments for that loan, with a variable interest rate of 5.51 percent.

As of June 2026, Botswana's public debt stood at approximately P95 billion, or 32.12 percent of GDP, including government guarantees. Direct government debt, excluding guarantees, was P86.33 billion, with successive loans carrying their own repayment schedules.

bw.headline: Botswana diamond workers allege exploitation
bw.dek: The Botswana Diamond Workers Union claims some firms pay meagre wages and force punishing hours on staff.
paragraphs: The Botswana Diamond Workers Union (BDWU) has accused some diamond cutting and polishing factories of exploiting workers, particularly Indian migrants. Allegations include meagre wages, precarious contracts, punishing hours, and intimidation against union organizing.

These claims emerge as Botswana's diamond trade faces soft global demand, sliding prices, and competition from lab-grown stones. The BDWU's accusations strike at the country's reputation for producing ethical diamonds, a brand built over nearly six decades.

Botswana sought to keep more value from its diamonds by developing local cutting and polishing, aiming to create jobs and transfer skills. However, operating costs in Botswana are higher than in established hubs like Surat, India, potentially leading some firms to cut labour costs.

bw.headline: Ukraine demands guarantees over captured Motswana
bw.dek: Botswana faces diplomatic hurdles in securing the release of a citizen fighting for Russia.
paragraphs: Ukraine wants assurances that a captured Motswana will not rejoin Russian forces, complicating Botswana’s negotiations to secure the citizen’s release.

Minister of International Relations Phenyo Butale told Ntlo ya Dikgosi on Monday that negotiations with Ukrainian authorities were progressing, but Kyiv remained concerned the captured person might return to the Russian military.

Butale was responding to a question from Kgosi Ian Khama of GaMangwato, explaining that Ukraine fears foreign nationals released after capture could rejoin Russia’s war effort. Botswana faces difficulty providing a firm guarantee about a citizen’s future conduct, and continued recruitment of Batswana into the Russian military further complicates efforts to reassure Ukraine.

More than 35 Burkinabe business people attended the expo to meet Indonesian counterparts, identify suppliers, and explore partnerships. This engagement follows the September 2026 signing of a framework cooperation agreement and a visa exemption accord for diplomatic and service passport holders.

The TEI 2026 serves as a platform to connect businesses and convert identified opportunities into concrete projects. The goal is to leverage Indonesia's industrial capabilities and Burkina Faso's economic transformation objectives for sustainable partnerships. The next TEI event is scheduled for 2027.

bf.headline: African cardiologists meet in Ouagadougou
bf.dek: The 9th International Congress of the Burkina Faso Cardiology Society and the 4th International Congress of the Association of Cardiology Societies of West and Central Africa are.
paragraphs: Ouagadougou is hosting the 9th International Congress of the Burkina Faso Cardiology Society and the 4th International Congress of the Association of Cardiology Societies of West and Central Africa from October 28 to 30, 2026. The dual scientific meeting, themed "Heart and Nutrition," brings together specialists from across Africa to discuss strategies for preventing and managing cardiovascular diseases. A key message from the experts is that heart health is built not only in hospitals but also in kitchens and through daily eating habits.

The congress aims to bridge scientific knowledge with the realities of African populations, focusing on how to reconcile socio-economic conditions and dietary traditions with effective cardiovascular prevention. According to the President of the Burkina Faso Cardiology Society, Pr Nobila Valentin Yaméogo, nutritional advice must be adapted to patients' daily lives and financial capacities. He stressed that effective prevention requires considering dietary habits and purchasing power.

Pr Nobila Valentin Yaméogo called for concrete proposals from the scientific exchanges to guide public policies and strengthen awareness campaigns, emphasizing the need to connect science with people and promote early nutritional education. Excessive salt consumption was identified as a primary risk factor at the congress opening.

bf.headline: Ouagadougou hosts tribute to Professor Idrissa Ouédraogo
bf.dek: Academics from Mali, Niger, Senegal, and Canada will join Burkinabe scholars to discuss informal sector development.
paragraphs: Universities Thomas-Sankara and Aube-Nouvelle, along with the Centre for Economic Integration Studies in Africa, are hosting an international conference in Ouagadougou from October 29-31, 2026, to honor Professor Idrissa Mohamed Ouédraogo. The event celebrates his career, which includes supervising 47 doctoral theses and training hundreds of professionals now working in public administration, banking, insurance, and regional organizations. The conference theme is 'Informal Sector and Development in Africa: Theoretical Issues and Action Perspectives'.

The gathering, under the patronage of Prime Minister Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo and sponsored by Minister Mathias Traoré and Isidore Kini, aims to recognize Professor Ouédraogo's over three decades of dedication to research and teaching. Researchers and practitioners from Mali, Niger, Senegal, and Canada will present scientific communications on topics such as formalizing the informal sector, mobile money's impact on poverty, and the effect of foreign aid on African economies.

The conference also features discussions on public borrowing and informal sector credit access within the UEMOA region. Professor Didier Zoungrana, president of Thomas-Sankara University, praised the initiative to honor Ouédraogo's contributions to human capital development and knowledge transmission. The organizing committee president, Professor Mahamadou Diarra, described the event as a way for students to repay their master's debt through scientific debate.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso explores nuclear tech for farming
bf.dek: Scientists and officials met in Ouagadougou to discuss how nuclear techniques can boost crop yields and improve soil and water management.
paragraphs: The Atomic Energy Agency of Burkina Faso (ABEA), with the Health Sciences Research Institute, held a conference in Ouagadougou on Wednesday about using nuclear technologies for productive and resilient agriculture. ABEA Director General Harouna Sawadogo stated the meeting aimed to share knowledge on how nuclear techniques can address current agricultural challenges.

Sawadogo explained that nuclear and isotopic techniques help understand soils, manage water and fertilizers better, and select higher-yielding crop varieties suited to Burkina Faso's climate. These technologies also offer solutions for pest control with reduced environmental impact and improve crop conservation and product quality.

University professor Ismaël Henry Bassolé presented how national yields could double or triple, enabling exports, and how specific rice varieties, like the local 'moui kolgho', can be developed for different dietary needs. He clarified that the process involves exposing seeds to energy, similar to medical X-rays, to modify genetic material.

bi.headline: Burundi farmers face fertilizer shortage
bi.dek: Farmers in Gitega report insufficient fertilizer distribution and delays in refunds for previous orders.
paragraphs: Burundian farmers in Gitega are struggling with a severe fertilizer shortage, jeopardizing the A 2026 growing season. Many farmers have not received adequate fertilizer since 2020, with some receiving none at all. This scarcity threatens crop yields and household incomes.

Joseph Hatungimana, 49, from Kibiri, criticized the unequal distribution and difficulties in reclaiming money paid for past orders. He stated that instead of receiving fertilizer, farmers are given tickets to get refunds from microfinance and commercial banks. Joselyne Manirambona, 30, from Jimbi, noted that the 16 kg of fertilizer provided is insufficient for her needs, requiring at least two Imbura bags and one urea bag.

Evariste Gahungu, 72, from Rweza hill, is still awaiting documents to recover funds from the A 2025 season, having received only 16 kg of fertilizer for A 2026 when he needs three bags. Farmers are concerned about food shortages if production is insufficient, with some considering organic compost as an alternative. They are calling on the government to allow private importers to increase fertilizer supply.

cm.headline: Cameroon power link to Chad costs CFA145 billion
cm.dek: Revised estimate covers 426km of transmission lines and substations for electricity exports.
paragraphs: Cameroon's section of the electricity interconnection with Chad will cost an estimated CFA145.2 billion for its first phase. This revised figure follows an October 12-16, 2026, assessment mission by the African Development Bank (AfDB) to review the project's restructuring. The works include 426 kilometers of high-voltage transmission lines and substations.

The Cameroonian team for the Cameroon-Chad Power Interconnection Project (PIRECT) stated the estimate covers Option 2-bis, the first phase of the restructuring plan. This cross-border component aims to enable electricity exports of 100 megawatts (MW) to Chad by 2030. The infrastructure includes 225-kilovolt (kV) transmission lines along the Wouro-Soua–Garoua II and Maroua–Chad border routes.

This CFA145.2 billion is an estimated project cost and not a new financing package from the AfDB. The planned works are separate from the connection between Cameroon's Southern and Northern Interconnected Grids.

cm.headline: Cameroon suspends opposition party for three months
cm.dek: Four opposition parties condemn the decision by the Minister of Territorial Administration, Paul Atanga Nji.
paragraphs: Cameroon's Minister of Territorial Administration, Paul Atanga Nji, suspended the Front for the National Salvation of Cameroon (FSNC) for three months on October 27. This decision, made one year after presidential elections and three months before legislative and municipal polls, has drawn condemnation from several opposition parties.

The UDC, PCRN, MANIDEM, and MP3 parties have voiced their disapproval, with the MP3 calling the suspension a serious hindrance to political freedoms and an attack on pluralism. MANIDEM suggests the ruling RDPC party uses authoritarian measures to secure electoral victories, while the UDC questions the timing and purpose of the suspension.

The PCRN urged the minister to reconsider the decision, stating that the country needs appeasement, not heightened tensions. The MP3 called for the Prime Minister to intervene in what they described as a political act, highlighting the FSNC's alleged violation of the republic's laws.

cm.headline: Cameroon secures €87 million for cocoa and coffee
cm.dek: The Green Climate Fund approved financing for a six-year program to boost agricultural output across five regions.
paragraphs: Cameroon will receive €87 million from the Green Climate Fund (GCF) to develop its cocoa and coffee sectors. The GCF Board approved the financing on October 27, 2026, as part of a €215.9 million program called Resilient Agriculture for Climate, Investment, Nature and Equity (RACINE). Cameroon's Ministry of Economy, Planning and Regional Development (MINEPAT) was accredited to oversee the project.

The RACINE program will run for six years and cover the Centre, South, East, Littoral, and South-West regions, with the Cocoa and Coffee Development Fund (FODECC) as the executing agency. Cameroon must contribute €88.5 million from export levies, and 90% of the GCF's €87 million, which is €78.3 million, will be provided as loans, with only €8.7 million as a grant.

The financing aims to significantly increase agricultural output, following a decline in cocoa sales. An additional €40.4 million in grants will come from the Central African Forest Initiative (CAFI) tied to results.

cm.headline: Blaise Kengne leads Barry Callebaut Cameroon
cm.dek: Kengne returns to Cameroon after leading Nigerian operations to head SIC Cacaos and Barry Callebaut Cameroon.
paragraphs: Blaise Kengne has been appointed chief executive officer of SIC Cacaos and Barry Callebaut Cameroon. Kengne returns to the country after leading Barry Callebaut Nigeria since October 2023.

Kengne brings over 18 years of experience, including previous roles at SIC Cacaos in Douala. His appointment occurs as SIC Cacaos received 40,012 tonnes of cocoa beans in the 2025–2026 season, a 14% decrease from the prior year.

Overall, Cameroon's industrial processors handled 95,946 tonnes of cocoa beans, down 13% from the previous season. SIC Cacaos, despite lower bean intake, remained the country's largest producer of processed cocoa products, making 29,245 tonnes.

cf.headline: Rotary Club supports polio response in Bangui
cf.dek: Community health workers trained to identify and report suspected polio cases following detection of two cases in Ouango.
paragraphs: The Rotary Club Bangui Douain Rénové and partners are supporting the Central African Republic's Ministry of Public Health in response to two polio cases detected in Ouango, Bangui. A training session for community health agents took place on Monday, October 26, to enhance surveillance and active case finding.

Émelien Gérard Nerguidima, representing the Rotary Club, stated that the training aims to equip agents to better identify suspected cases in their neighborhoods and refer them to health facilities. These agents, living within the communities, are crucial for early detection and public awareness of polio prevention measures. Nerguidima noted that the presence of two cases suggests potentially more within the community.

Since the start of 2026, seven polio cases have been recorded in the Central African Republic, with two of these in Ouango. This initiative, extending beyond World Polio Day on October 24, involves the Ministry of Public Health, Rotary Club, WHO, and UNICEF in the global polio eradication effort.

cf.headline: Amnesty International warns of special court closure
cf.dek: The Central African Republic's special court risks closure by 2028 due to a lack of funding.
paragraphs: Amnesty International has alerted that the Special Criminal Court (CPS) in the Central African Republic faces closure by 2028 due to insufficient funding. The organization stated that only the UN and EU are currently providing financial support to the court, which is tasked with prosecuting war crimes and crimes against humanity. This lack of funds has forced the court to halt investigations, leaving alleged perpetrators of international crimes potentially free.

The CPS relies exclusively on voluntary contributions from states and international organizations. In 2025, the United States withdrew its financial support, leaving over $4.15 million in unpaid commitments. This funding crisis led the court to dismiss a quarter of its staff, including foreign experts, between August and September 2025, impacting its witness protection unit.

Amnesty International is calling on Central African authorities, the UN, the EU, and partner states to provide or continue financial support for the CPS's operational budget. The court's national counterparts reportedly lack the resources and independence to handle these complex cases.

km.headline: Comoros drafts 2035 migration policy
km.dek: The plan aims to unify migration governance, protect rights, and leverage diaspora resources for development.
paragraphs: The Union of Comoros is developing a national migration policy, with a first draft presented on October 29, 2026. Minister of Interior Mohamed Ahmed Assoumani led a meeting where the document, created with the International Organization for Migration (IOM), was discussed. The policy aims to balance national sovereignty with migrant protection and economic growth.

The project, presented by national consultant Moctar Zouboudou, outlines eight objectives for unified and sustainable migration governance by 2035. Key goals include strengthening institutions and legal frameworks, enhancing inter-agency coordination, and protecting migrants' fundamental rights. It also focuses on preventing irregular migration and combating human trafficking.

The policy also seeks to organize returns and promote safe, regular mobility channels. A significant component is mobilizing the Comorian diaspora's financial resources and skills for national development. Other planned orientations include adapting to climate crises, improving migration data, and fostering international partnerships.

km.headline: Comoros plans national cancer strategy
km.dek: Health officials met in Moroni to draft a strategic plan to combat cancer, aiming for improved care by December.
paragraphs: Comoros health officials met in Moroni from October 20-22, 2026, to develop a national cancer control strategy with support from the WHO and UNICEF. The meeting aimed to assess current capabilities and prepare a strategic plan expected in December. This initiative addresses the lack of a national cancer registry, which prevents precise tracking of patients, diagnoses, treatments, and outcomes.

Estimates from Globocan suggest 619 new cancer cases and 418 deaths in 2022, with uterine, prostate, and breast cancers being most frequent. The country currently lacks an operational radiotherapy service, on-site pathologists, and standardized chemotherapy protocols, often necessitating costly medical evacuations for patients. Questions remain about the selection process, state and family costs, and care for those unable to travel.

The planned strategy prioritizes better organization of medical evacuations, strengthening island-based care, and establishing a national cancer registry. Monthly remote medical consultations are proposed for Comorian doctors to consult with foreign specialists on complex cases. Dr. Saïd Mohamed Soulé noted that agreements with specialized foreign hospitals will be sought, with a pilot project planned within six months and a first oncology unit hoped for within a year.

km.headline: Comorian man died one hour after TikTok live
km.dek: Kassim, known as Mkataba, was killed in a car accident in Marseille on October 15.
paragraphs: Kassim, known online as Mkataba, finished a TikTok live stream at 23:34 on October 14, 2026. An hour and six minutes later, around 00:40 on October 15, he was involved in a fatal accident on the A7 motorway in Marseille. His family confirmed his death on October 23.

The TikTok live, broadcast from the account @mkatabao, began at 22:59 and lasted 35 minutes. Mkataba was struck by an Audi RS3 in the Plombières area, travelling at high speed towards Aix-en-Provence. Witnesses reported the vehicle was moving very fast, and the pedestrian died at the scene.

Previous reports suggested Mkataba was alive after the accident, but no verified testimony supports these claims. While Mkataba had received death threats on social media, no evidence links these threats to his death or implicates members of the Comorian community.

cg.headline: UBA Congo clients must update accounts by December 2026
cg.dek: The bank requires updated personal and business documents to ensure security and regulatory compliance.
paragraphs: UBA Congo is asking all individual and business clients to update their account files by December 31, 2026. This action is part of the bank's commitment to secure banking operations and meet regulatory requirements. A complete and current client file helps the bank maintain reliable information, secure banking relationships, and prevent fraud.

Individual clients need a valid ID and updated personal and professional information, with recent proof of address if necessary. Business clients must provide up-to-date legal and administrative documents, details on directors and beneficial owners, and proof of business activity. Clients can visit their UBA branch or contact their account manager to complete these updates.

Updating client files strengthens account security, streamlines operations, and ensures transparent banking relationships. The bank urges clients not to wait until the last moment to verify and update their information before the 2026 deadline.

ci.headline: Ivory Coast simulates major cyberattack
ci.dek: 800 participants from energy, telecoms, and finance faced a fictional digital crisis in Abidjan.
paragraphs: The first national cyber crisis simulation, CYBER.EX 2026, began on Wednesday, October 28, in Port-Bouët, Ivory Coast. The National Agency for Information Systems Security (ANSSI) organized the exercise where 800 participants from the energy, telecoms, and finance sectors faced a large-scale, fictional cyberattack. The teams in Abidjan were tasked with managing a crisis, making quick decisions, coordinating efforts, and maintaining services under virtual assault.

ANSSI Director General, Brigadier General Guelpétchin Ouattara, stated that participants would test their collective capabilities in real conditions against a major cyber crisis. The exercise focuses on four skills: piloting, decision-making, coordination, and business continuity. Minister Mamadou Touré, speaking on behalf of the Vice-Prime Minister and Minister of Defence, described cyberspace as a new battlefield and a domain of confrontation, emphasizing that a vulnerability in a neighboring country could become their own.

The simulation aims to improve collaboration among national cybersecurity ecosystem actors, who rarely convene. Minister of Digital Transition, Djibril Ouattara, highlighted cybersecurity as a key state policy instrument. A Senegalese delegation's presence indicated Abidjan's intention to share its experience and contribute to West Africa's collective security, according to Mamadou Touré.

ci.headline: Ivory Coast trains 26 experts on Chemical Weapons protection
ci.dek: Specialists from 14 francophone nations are learning detection, decontamination, and victim care at the AILCT.
paragraphs: 26 experts from 14 countries are undergoing advanced training in chemical weapons protection in Ivory Coast since October 27, 2026. The course, organized with the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) at the International Academy for Counter-Terrorism (AILCT), concludes on November 3 with an integrated exercise.

For eight days, trainees are practicing detection, decontamination, emergency management, and victim care, moving from theory to practical application. Loic Luyeye, OPCW representative, noted that while Africa is free of chemical weapons, toxic substances used daily in agriculture, industry, and mining pose constant risks. A factory leak or poorly managed pesticide stock can severely impact populations.

The training, a joint effort by the OPCW, the Permanent Secretariat of the Ivorian Commission for the Prohibition of Weapons of Mass Destruction (SPCIADM-CI), and the AILCT, aims to strengthen regional protection capacities. Participants will return with skills to identify hazardous substances, isolate areas, decontaminate individuals, and organize their care, reinforcing counter-terrorism efforts for exposed states.

ci.headline: Abidjan hospital performs three arterial surgeries
ci.dek: Institut Cœur de Grâce uses a hybrid operating room and French specialists to treat vascular conditions and train local doctors.
paragraphs: The Institut Cœur de Grâce (ICG) in Abidjan successfully operated on three patients for arterial blockages between October 26 and 28, 2026. Procedures included replacing an aortic valve, performing a coronary bypass, and treating a coarctation of the ascending aorta. The hospital utilized its latest-generation hybrid operating room for these interventions.

French specialists collaborated with ICG to conduct the surgeries and train Ivorian doctors in vascular procedures. Hospital officials stated this mission advances cardiovascular surgery and local medical capabilities. They also stressed the importance of early detection and regular cardiology check-ups for the population.

The ICG aims to improve access to cardiovascular care in Ivory Coast and the sub-region through its facilities and specialized equipment. The development of such interventions is a major challenge for the health system, as cardiovascular diseases require rapid diagnosis and appropriate management.

eg.headline: El-Sisi in Moscow for Russia-Africa Summit
eg.dek: Egypt and Russia will discuss economic cooperation, investment, and food security at the summit.
paragraphs: President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi arrived in Moscow on October 28 for the third Russia-Africa Summit, where he will meet Russian President Vladimir Putin. The summit, running from October 28-29, aims to expand cooperation and economic opportunities between African nations and Russia. Discussions are expected to cover trade, investment, energy, agriculture, security, and technology.

Egypt and Russia have strengthened economic ties, with bilateral trade reaching approximately USD 10.5 billion in 2025, more than double the 2021 figure. Key exchanges include Russian wheat and metal products for Egyptian fruit and vegetables. Russia's state nuclear company, Rosatom, is also constructing the El Dabaa nuclear power plant in Egypt.

This meeting follows previous summits in Sochi in 2019 and St. Petersburg in 2023. Egypt is a significant economic partner for Russia in Africa, with cooperation extending to industrial development and energy supplies.

eg.headline: Egypt eyes floating nuclear reactors with Russia
eg.dek: Cairo is discussing the deployment of floating and small modular nuclear reactors with Rosatom.
paragraphs: Egypt is in talks with Russia's Rosatom to potentially deploy floating and small modular nuclear reactors (SMRs). These floating plants can generate electricity and thermal energy while also providing large-scale seawater desalination. The discussions signal a potential expansion of Egypt's nuclear strategy beyond the El-Dabaa project.

Rosatom Chief Executive Officer Alexey Likhachev confirmed active discussions on floating nuclear power plants and compact land-based reactors. Floating nuclear power plants are compact reactor units on vessels or offshore barges, designed for coastlines and remote regions without extensive onshore infrastructure. Russia operates the world's first floating nuclear power plant, Akademik Lomonosov, powered by two KLT-40S reactors.

These mobile reactors, potentially based on Rosatom's RITM-200 series, would supply reliable power and desalinated water to Egypt's coastal municipalities and industrial zones. This initiative supports national energy security and carbon reduction goals. Interest in floating nuclear technology is growing globally due to rising baseload power demand from industrial electrification and data centers.

eg.headline: Egypt moves to raise fines for false news
eg.dek: The government is preparing amendments to the Penal Code to increase penalties for spreading false information online.
paragraphs: Egypt’s Cabinet announced on Wednesday, October 28, that it is preparing amendments to the Penal Code to increase fines for false news and rumour-related offences. This action is part of a larger government plan to regulate social media through new digital safety legislation, expanded technical monitoring, and public awareness campaigns.

Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly directed the formation of a working group to follow up on recommendations from a committee examining harmful social media practices. Justice Minister Mahmoud El-Sherif presented a report to the Cabinet on measures to safeguard Egyptian family values and social cohesion.

The committee also proposed establishing general rules for digital platforms through forthcoming digital safety legislation and stronger state oversight. The government has not yet specified the proposed fines or announced a timetable for introducing the amendments.

eg.headline: Egypt's pensions fall short for 10.2 million elderly
eg.dek: Retirees say modest, unevenly distributed benefits do not cover living costs as the older population grows.
paragraphs: Egypt's elderly population has reached 10.2 million people, a rise from 9.8 million a year ago, according to the national statistics agency.  These 10.2 million citizens aged 60 and older face modest and uneven social protections, with many retirees finding pensions insufficient for a dignified life. The government has introduced new measures including pensions, a cash program for the poor, a rights law, and health insurance reforms.

Despite government efforts, critics including unions, lawmakers, and researchers argue that pension payments are too low and eligibility criteria are becoming stricter.  The minimum pension for new retirees increased to EGP 1,755 (USD 31) in January, and existing pensions saw a 15 percent rise on July 1, costing an estimated EGP 70 billion (USD 1.25 billion) annually.  However, these amounts are considered inadequate by many.

The older population in Egypt is projected to constitute roughly 14 percent of the total by 2050. Unions and researchers point out that some promised benefits remain largely on paper. The state's minimum wage for public-sector workers is also a point of contention in discussions about adequate support for the elderly.

eg.headline: Suez Canal Authority seeks Greek maritime investment
eg.dek: Egypt's canal authority chairman met with Greece's ambassador to discuss trade and logistics cooperation.
paragraphs: Suez Canal Authority Chairman Ossama Rabiee met with Greece’s Ambassador Nikolaos Papageorgiou at SCA headquarters in Ismailia to discuss strengthening bilateral cooperation in trade and logistics investment. Rabiee invited Greek commercial enterprises to engage more actively with Egypt’s maritime corridor and cooperate with the SCA, highlighting the authority's developed industrial base and new maritime services.

Rabiee stated the Suez Canal has managed crises and safeguarded global supply chains by working with the maritime community. Papageorgiou praised the canal's progress as an ongoing success story and an indispensable artery of global trade, expressing hope for regional geopolitical stability. He noted steady shipping through the canal is vital for global supply chains.

The meeting aims to attract more investment in projects in the canal region, particularly for Greek shipowners who control one of the world's largest merchant fleets. SCA facilities could offer ship repair and dry-docking as alternatives to Greek and Turkish yards, while bunkering services could generate recurring revenue. Suez Canal revenue reached $567.1 million in August 2026, with 1,358 vessels transiting.

gq.headline: Equatorial Guinea joins Russia-Africa summit action plan
gq.dek: Leaders agreed a joint action plan for 2027-2029 and discussed economic cooperation.
paragraphs: Equatorial Guinea's President Obiang Nguema Mbasogo participated in the final day of the III Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow on October 29, 2026. The summit's activities took place in the Grand Kremlin Palace, featuring plenary sessions chaired by Russian President Vladimir Putin and African Union Chair Évariste Ndayishimiye of Burundi. Discussions covered Russia-Africa relations, Africa's international role, and expanding economic, political, technological, and humanitarian cooperation.

A key outcome was the planned approval of a final declaration on Russian-African relations, a declaration on artificial intelligence cooperation, and a joint action plan for 2027-2029. Several cooperation agreements and memorandums between Russia and African nations were also set to be signed. President Mbasogo's attendance continued his Moscow agenda, which included participation in the Gas Exporting Countries Forum and a bilateral meeting with Vladimir Putin.

The summit concluded with a joint press conference by the Presidents of Russia and Burundi, detailing the meeting's main results. Part of the declarations focused on Africa's economic transformation, industrial development, and establishing result-oriented alliances.

AFODECA seeks to embed prevention as a daily practice for citizens, moving beyond institutional responsibility. This initiative marks the beginning of a project to enhance Equatorial Guinea's alliances and response capacity to disaster risks.

gq.headline: Equatorial Guinea Senate approves press freedom law
gq.dek: The new regulation aims to protect journalists, establish clear duties, and promote rigorous reporting.
paragraphs: The Senate in Equatorial Guinea has approved a new law regulating press freedom, recognizing journalism as a pillar of the state and a public service. The law focuses on three key areas: protecting journalists' security, rights, and dignity; regulating professional duties and ethics; and demanding rigor and continuous training.

The Secretary of State for Information, Press, Culture, and Tourism expressed gratitude for the law, stating it resulted from dialogue with journalists, media directors, civil society, and students. The Democratic Coalition Group voted in favor, emphasizing the need for editorial independence, fair labor practices, media funding transparency, and institutional guarantees.

The PDGE Parliamentary Group also supported the bill, with its spokesperson warning about the dangers of fake news and hate speech on social media. The Senate president highlighted the importance of good journalistic practices, adherence to truth, and social responsibility to foster national development and cohesion.

gq.headline: BEAC sets deadline for old CFA franc coins
gq.dek: Central African states have one year to exchange old 1 to 500 CFA franc coins for new currency.
paragraphs: The Bank of Central African States (BEAC) has set a one-year deadline for exchanging old 1 to 500 CFA franc coins across the CEMAC region. This decision, made by the UMAC Ministerial Committee, aims to streamline currency circulation. The exchange period begins on November 1, 2026, and concludes on October 31, 2027.

During the first phase, from November 1, 2026, to July 31, 2027, individuals can exchange the old coins at BEAC branches, commercial banks, and microfinance institutions. The second phase, from August 1 to October 31, 2027, limits exchanges to BEAC offices only, with no limit on the amount for individuals and businesses. Commercial banks and microfinance institutions are obligated to accept these coins from the public, regardless of customer status.

After October 31, 2027, the old coins will no longer be redeemable. The BEAC has urged financial intermediaries to establish necessary mechanisms to facilitate the exchange process and prevent citizens from losing the value of their old currency due to lack of information or procedural difficulties. Coins from the 2006 and 2024 series remain legal tender.

gq.headline: Cronos Airlines cancels Malabo flights
gq.dek: Passengers stranded at Malabo airport face uncertainty as technical issues ground flights to Bata.
paragraphs: Cronos Airlines cancelled flights from Malabo to Bata on Thursday, leaving passengers stranded at the airport. Passengers were informed on Tuesday to stop checking in and go to company offices, later receiving confirmation of cancellations. Some passengers who bought tickets on Tuesday were still sold tickets despite ongoing cancellations.

A passenger showed a message received on Thursday, October 29, stating flight 901 to Bata was rescheduled due to a technical problem, with no new departure time given. Passengers who bought tickets directly from Cronos agencies were told they would receive a message, while those who used third-party agencies had their phone numbers taken for updates.

Passengers expressed concern about when they would be able to travel and some are considering seeking refunds to travel by boat. The suspension of Ceiba Intercontinental flights, due to aircraft reviews, further limits air transport options between Malabo and Bata. Cronos Airlines passengers were still awaiting confirmed travel dates and clear information on flight resumption.

er.headline: US lifts sanctions on Eritrea
er.dek: Sanctions removed on September 19, 2026, targeted the ruling party's financial and military apparatus.
paragraphs: The United States removed sanctions on Eritrea on September 19, 2026. These sanctions were imposed in 2021 due to Eritrea’s involvement in the Tigray War. The US government had outlined plans to lift the sanctions four months prior, according to a Reuters report.

Human rights groups criticized the decision, citing Eritrea's record of forced labor and torture under the ruling People’s Front for Democracy and Justice (PFDJ). Eritrea's government called the sanctions 'illicit and immoral' and claimed they caused 'incalculable damage' and constrained development.

The removed sanctions targeted the PFDJ’s financial and military bodies and two officials, Abraha Kassa and Hagos Gebrehiwet. The Eritrean Defence Force’s chief of staff, Filipos Woldeyohannes, remains under separate sanctions. The PFDJ has previously benefited from the removal of UN sanctions in 2018, remaining self-sufficient.

ke.headline: Husband arrested over wife's shallow grave burial
ke.dek: Detectives in Kajiado County arrested Shon David Rabassa Kioko after a farmhand reported the incident.
paragraphs: Detectives in Isinya, Kajiado County, arrested Shon David Rabassa Kioko on October 30, 2026, for allegedly murdering his 34-year-old wife, Farida Peter Sangka. Her body was found buried in a shallow grave on their farm in Entarakuet.

The arrest followed a report by farmhand Ndayishimiye Deo, a Burundian national, who stated Kioko instructed him to help bury the body. Police officers secured the scene and exhumed the remains in the presence of a pathologist for forensic examination.
The body was moved to Nairobi Funeral Home pending a postmortem examination. Kioko and Deo remain in custody as the Directorate of Criminal Investigations pursues justice for Sangka’s family.

ke.headline: Kenya launches pesticide residue monitoring framework
ke.dek: New system aims to improve food safety and protect horticultural exports from rejections.
paragraphs: Kenya has launched its National Pesticide Residue Monitoring Framework (NPRMF) to coordinate pesticide testing and data sharing across the agricultural sector. The framework aims to support regulatory oversight, food safety compliance, consumer protection, and access to domestic and export markets. The Pest Control Products Board, the Kenya Plant Health Inspectorate Service, and the Agriculture and Food Authority helped develop it.

Agriculture Secretary James Wanjohi said at the October 15 Nairobi launch that food control is multisectoral, emphasizing working together from farm to fork. The framework matters for exporters because Kenya's horticultural exports have been rejected at European borders for exceeding pesticide residue limits, particularly for beans and peas. A coordinated system provides a single reference for testing data, enabling exporters to demonstrate compliance and regulators to identify problem areas before shipments reach markets.

The framework's development involved over two years of consultations and stakeholder engagement. A pilot phase in five counties from May to June 2025 identified capacity gaps before the national rollout. Continued support from governments and development partners is sought for sustained funding of laboratory equipment, staff training, and sample collection.

ke.headline: Kenya develops national coffee flavour atlas
ke.dek: The initiative will document diverse coffee profiles from 34 counties, with findings published in 2027.
paragraphs: Kenya's coffee industry is creating a national flavour atlas to document diverse coffee profiles across the country. The Kenya Coffee Flavor Map initiative will analyze approximately 500 samples from 34 coffee-growing counties, with results expected in 2027. This project aims to connect specific flavour characteristics with regional origins, varieties, and production methods.

Producers, co-operatives, researchers, and sensory professionals are collaborating on the initiative, which involves blind sensory evaluations by Kenyan and international coffee cuppers. The findings will be made freely available to the industry and will be a central feature of the Kenya Coffee Flavor & Origin Expo in Nairobi from November 14-16. Professional cupping sessions are scheduled for November 15 and 16.

The planned atlas will include regional flavour profiles, visual maps, and a searchable database to showcase the diversity of Kenyan coffee. Marty Pollack, co-founder of Torch Coffee, stated the project will foster collaboration between Kenyan and international coffee professionals. The initiative is supported by the Government of Kenya, the Coffee Board of Kenya, and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) in Kenya.

ke.headline: CIP and Crop Trust develop climate-resilient potatoes in Kenya
ke.dek: The BOLD project will use wild potato relatives to breed varieties resistant to heat, unpredictable rain, pests, and diseases.
paragraphs: The International Potato Center (CIP) and the Crop Trust have launched a new phase of the BOLD project in Kenya to develop climate-resilient potato varieties. This initiative aims to strengthen seed systems and improve farmers’ access to quality planting material.

The project will harness genetic traits from wild potato relatives to help breeders develop varieties capable of withstanding rising temperatures, unpredictable rainfall, pests, and diseases. Dr. Benjamin Kilian, BOLD Project Coordinator at the Crop Trust, stated that wild relatives contain options agriculture needs as conditions change.

Potatoes are Kenya's second most important staple after maize, supporting 3.3 million jobs and contributing US$324 million annually, but production faces pressure from climate change and diseases. The goal is to release at least one improved variety in Kenya combining climate resilience, disease resistance, and high yields.

za.headline: South Africa reach 140/4 against Australia
za.dek: Proteas hold a 40-run lead after Australia were bowled out for 429 in the third Test in Cape Town.
paragraphs: South Africa ended day three of the third Test against Australia in Cape Town on Thursday at 140/4, leading by 40 runs. Matthew Breetzke was 19 not out and Ryan Rickelton was unbeaten on eight. Australia were bowled out for 429 in their first innings, a lead of 100 runs.

Spin bowler Simon Harmer led the Proteas attack with 4/104, removing Josh Inglis (102) and Alex Carey (80) who had put on 185 runs for the fifth wicket. Seamer Marco Jansen took 3/60 as South Africa's bowlers claimed the last five Australian wickets for 59 runs. Captain Temba Bavuma scored 31 off 115 balls before being bowled by Nathan Lyon.

The Proteas need a strong performance on day four to stay in the series, which is currently level at 1-1. Bavuma and Marques Ackerman (62) attempted to stabilise the innings after South Africa fell to 95/3. Wiaan Mulder, Marco Jansen, and Simon Harmer are still to bat for the hosts.

za.headline: Lesufi and Zille trade barbs over Joburg service delivery
za.dek: Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi and DA mayoral candidate Helen Zille exchanged insults ahead of local elections.
paragraphs: Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi and DA mayoral candidate Helen Zille traded insults on Thursday over service delivery in Johannesburg. Lesufi referred to Zille as a "Ford Cortina," an old car, while Zille accused Lesufi of taking credit for a transformer replacement in Soweto that the DA had funded. Johannesburg faces a R220 billion infrastructure backlog and less than half of its service delivery targets are being met.

Zille claimed on X that the DA had paid for the transformer and arranged its installation with Eskom, criticizing Lesufi for claiming credit. Lesufi responded by sharing older posts on X, stating he had been involved with transformers since 2024 and that the Gauteng government invested R82 million for transformers this year alone. He mentioned opening two in Snake Park and one in Rietvallei, with three more planned for Kagiso.

The exchange occurred as the battle for the City of Johannesburg intensifies ahead of local government elections. Disgruntled residents have protested deteriorating municipal services, including power and water outages, potholes, drug activity, and crime. The contest involves severe municipal decay, a large Eskom debt, and clashes between the ANC and opposition parties like the DA and ActionSA.

za.headline: South Africans debate realistic SASSA grant increase
za.dek: Some citizens favour a smaller, achievable rise in the old-age grant over larger, unmet promises.
paragraphs: South Africans are discussing a proposed increase to the SASSA old-age grant, with some favouring a R3 000 monthly amount as more realistic. Detlef Weber commented on The South African’s Facebook page that this figure strikes a balance, unlike calls for R5 000 or R6 000 grants. Tania Steenkamp added that even an extra R600 monthly is valuable for pensioners.

Grant recipients who depend solely on the payment could use additional funds for groceries, transport, or utility bills. Those supporting a moderate rise believe the government is more likely to approve an amount that fits current budget constraints. The debate acknowledges that the current grant struggles to keep pace with rising food and electricity prices.

Any adjustment to grant amounts requires announcement by the Minister of Finance in the February Budget Speech, with changes effective from April. Until then, current payment rates remain. The South African reported that 41% of the population receives a grant today, up from 25% in 2006.

za.headline: Stellenbosch mother dies after son killed in crash
za.dek: Gaynor Adams, 38, died in hospital five days after her six-year-old son died at the scene of a crash on Helshoogte Pass.
paragraphs: A Stellenbosch mother, Gaynor Adams, 38, died in Tygerberg Hospital on Tuesday, October 27, after sustaining critical injuries in a crash five days earlier. Her six-year-old son, Berto-Lee Adams, died at the scene of the collision on Helshoogte Pass on Thursday, October 22. The mother and son were travelling from Kylemore towards Idas Valley when their vehicle collided with another car.

Stellenbosch municipal spokesperson Stuart Grobbelaar stated that a white sedan travelling towards Stellenbosch lost control and collided with a silver Toyota. Emergency personnel attended to Gaynor Adams at the scene before transporting her to hospital, while paramedics found Berto-Lee near the vehicle and declared him dead. The occupants of the second vehicle were not injured.

Cloetesville police have registered a culpable homicide case and are investigating the circumstances surrounding the fatal crash. St Idas Primary School, where Berto-Lee was a learner, and Speelkring Pre-Primary, where he attended an after-school programme, have both expressed shock and extended condolences to the family.

za.headline: Cape Town terminal expects 13% fruit export rise
za.dek: South Africa's deciduous fruit exports, including grapes and stone fruit, face new delivery rules for the upcoming season.
paragraphs: The Cape Town Container Terminal anticipates a 13% increase in South Africa’s deciduous fruit export volumes for the 2026/27 season, running from November to April. This growth, expected to reach 13% compared to the prior season, involves table grapes, plums, peaches, and apricots primarily destined for European markets.

To manage the anticipated surge, the terminal has implemented new measures following engagements with industry stakeholders and Transport Minister Barbara Creecy. These include hiring extra staff, enhancing leave management, and establishing a 24-hour hotline, alongside a fixed weekly vessel schedule with a 21-day berthing plan. Exporters must now deliver 95% of refrigerated containers by stack closure to avoid missing vessels.

These changes follow a challenging 2025/26 season where operational issues at Cape Town diverted an estimated 55,000 tons of table grapes. The terminal has since reduced average vessel waiting time from 115 hours to 44.3 hours and ship turnaround time from 103 hours to 55 hours. The terminal also added 28 new rubber-tyred gantry cranes and four straddle carriers.

ng.headline: Court sacks Uzodinma as APC senatorial candidate
ng.dek: Federal High Court orders INEC to recognise Rochas Okorocha as APC candidate for Imo West election.
paragraphs: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Thursday nullified Governor Hope Uzodinma's candidacy for the APC in the Imo West Senatorial election scheduled for January 16, 2027. Justice Obiora Egwuatu ruled that Uzodinma was not the valid winner of the APC primary election held on May 18, which was monitored by INEC.

The court found that former governor Senator Rochas Okorocha secured the highest votes in the primary and should have been nominated. Justice Egwuatu ordered INEC to recognise Okorocha and publish his name as the APC candidate, barring Uzodinma from presenting himself as the party's choice.
The ruling follows a primary election monitored by INEC. Senator Okorocha was declared the winner by the court, while Governor Uzodinma was barred from presenting himself as the candidate.

ng.headline: Nigerian households weigh timing over rates for savings
ng.dek: Money not spent today has a purpose, influencing investment choices for Nigerian households and businesses.
paragraphs: Nigerian households and businesses face a key decision when saving temporarily unused funds: timing is more important than the interest rate offered. Money set aside is typically earmarked for future expenses such as rent, school fees, taxes, or emergencies.

This approach suggests that the immediate need for funds dictates savings strategy, rather than solely pursuing the highest yield. The purpose of the money influences how long it can be invested and the type of account chosen.
Understanding these short-term needs is crucial for effective financial planning. The decision-making process prioritizes accessibility and planned expenditures over maximizing returns on idle cash.

gh.headline: Mahama visits kente exhibition in Moscow
gh.dek: Ghana's president commended Russia-Ghana Parliamentary Forum for cultural exchange at the Russia-Africa Summit.
paragraphs: President John Dramani Mahama visited a Kente Exhibition in Moscow on Thursday, organised by the Russia-Ghana Parliamentary Forum. The exhibition, part of the Third Russia-Africa Summit, showcases Ghana's traditional textiles and cultural heritage. The Ghana Export Promotion Authority and Ghana’s Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry collaborated on the event.

Mahama praised the Russian Parliamentary Group for their friendship, stating that people-to-people relationships are more enduring than government ties. He highlighted the importance of understanding each other's cultures to consolidate these relationships. The President noted that nearly 11,000 people had visited the exhibition, which included explanations translated into Russian.

The exhibition aims to promote Ghana's cultural heritage through kente, an internationally recognized textile. President Mahama expressed appreciation for bringing the exhibition to Moscow, emphasizing the value of cultural understanding between nations.

gh.headline: Carrick keeps Fernandes as Manchester United captain
gh.dek: Michael Carrick confirmed Bruno Fernandes will continue as captain after clear-the-air talks following a recent dip in form.
paragraphs: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick stated Bruno Fernandes will remain captain of the club. Carrick benched Fernandes for the recent 3-0 loss to Bournemouth after the midfielder questioned team tactics following a Champions League defeat. Carrick and Fernandes held talks on Tuesday to address the situation and move forward.

Carrick said the decision to bench Fernandes was for football reasons and that the player is fully committed to the club. He confirmed there was no decision to be made about Fernandes' captaincy, stating the 32-year-old cares deeply about the team. Carrick's own position has been under scrutiny after the club's worst start to a Premier League season.

Despite speculation, Carrick will continue to lead the team and does not require assurances about his long-term security. Manchester United has gone eight games without a win, their worst run since the 2015-16 season. The club's chief executive and director of football met this week to discuss next steps.

gh.headline: GAFET donates fertiliser for Farmers' Day
gh.dek: The Ghana Agricultural Fund for Education and Transformation provided 1,000 bags of organic fertiliser for the 42nd National Farmers’ Day.
paragraphs: The Ghana Agricultural Fund for Education and Transformation (GAFET) donated 1,000 bags of 10-kilogramme organic fertiliser for the upcoming 42nd National Farmers’ Day celebration in December. The donation aims to support the recognition of farmers, especially young people, for their contributions to food production.

GAFET Lead Coordinator, Mr Steven Nhyira Odarteifio, presented the fertiliser to the Ministry of Food and Agriculture in Accra yesterday. He stated the gesture supports government efforts to reward farmers and was motivated by contributions from patriots towards the event. Mr Odarteifio, who is also the incoming National Youth Organiser for the NDC, highlighted the need for policies addressing youth aspirations in agriculture.

Mr Odarteifio encouraged more young people to embrace organic agriculture and sustainable farming practices. He noted that supporting farmers with inputs motivates them to sustain efforts towards improving food production. The Chairman of the National Farmers’ Day Celebration Committee, Mr John Dumelo, received the donation and expressed gratitude.

gh.headline: Four remanded over Worawora disturbances
gh.dek: Kwame Aboagye Ahenkora, Prince Asante, Daniel Wiafe, and Kwabena Nsimbo were detained following violence over festival rites.
paragraphs: The Dambai Circuit Court has remanded four individuals into police custody for their alleged role in disturbances at Dwabrem-Worawora in the Oti Region. Kwame Aboagye Ahenkora, 55, Prince Asante, 27, Daniel Wiafe, 20, and Kwabena Nsimbo, 22, are accused of involvement in the events that occurred on October 24, 2026.

The disturbances reportedly involved the burning of vehicle tyres amid claims of a High Court injunction against the Akwantutenten Festival rites, according to Deputy Superintendent of Police John Nchor. Police personnel extinguished fires and restored order, and the Oti Regional Security Council has directed disputing parties to seek resolution through the courts and Houses of Chiefs.

The accused will reappear before the court on November 17, 2026, as the Regional Police Command appeals for calm and respect for lawful processes. The Regional Security Council stressed that the chieftaincy dispute must be resolved through legal means.

The report highlights the ADF's involvement in the DRC's gold trade. The Sentry's analysis aims to uncover the financial flows that support the ADF's operations. The organization seeks to hold accountable those who facilitate the laundering of conflict gold.

Separately, in Ituri province, a military position in Bule-centre, Djugu territory, was attacked on October 29. cd.headline: Kinshasa parents worry over children's sugar intake
cd.dek: Health professionals warn of dental cavities, overweight, and type 2 diabetes risks from sweets sold near schools.
paragraphs: Excessive sugar consumption among children is causing concern for parents and health workers in Kinshasa. Sweets and sugary drinks, available from 100 Congolese francs near schools and in local shops, are easily accessible to young children, making it difficult for some parents to limit their intake.

A 10-year-old boy consumes sweets 90% of the time, actively seeking them out despite his mother's health advice. Other parents struggle with enforcement, acknowledging that children will consume sweets when unsupervised outside the home. Dr. Louise Hanyange, deputy director of the diabetes control program, highlighted risks including dental cavities, overweight, and obesity, which can lead to type 2 diabetes.

Dr. Hanyange recommends parents reduce children's daily sugar intake and offer water, fruits, and unsweetened beverages instead. The health professionals' warnings were shared on Thursday, October 29.

cd.headline: 26 deaths reported in Bunia amid Ebola fears
cd.dek: Community leaders in Bankoko, Bunia, report over a hundred contacts and 26 deaths in three weeks.
paragraphs: Community leaders in Bunia's Bankoko neighborhood reported 26 deaths and over a hundred contacts in nearly three weeks, raising fears of an Ebola resurgence. The figures, as of October 28, have not been confirmed by health authorities, who stated they are implementing preventative measures.

The deaths reportedly began after a woman returned from Djugu territory, where she attended a funeral. She died after being taken to a private clinic, and her body was returned home without precautions before burial, leading to further deaths among those in contact with the deceased.

Bunia's health zone chief, Dr. Prosper Ukurfwa, did not confirm the reported numbers but assured that surveillance, contact identification, patient transfer to treatment centers, and public awareness of barrier measures are underway.

tz.headline: Tanzania and Angola sign four cooperation deals
tz.dek: Leaders aim to transform 50 years of solidarity into practical economic ties with new agreements.
paragraphs: Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu Hassan and Angolan President João Manuel Lourenço signed four cooperation agreements in Dar es Salaam on Thursday, October 29. The deals aim to convert 50 years of solidarity into tangible economic links, addressing the slow progress in trade since formal relations began.

Agreements covered the transfer of sentenced persons and air services, with new memoranda on information and communications technology and meteorology. President Lourenço stated that African nations need stronger intra-continental ties to achieve development goals, noting that economic and trade relations between Tanzania and Angola remain very small.

Tanzania will reopen its embassy in Angola and appoint an ambassador to boost bilateral relations. The leaders agreed to organize a trade and investment forum to identify business opportunities, following President Samia's 2025 visit to Angola which also sought to reset economic cooperation.

tz.headline: Tanzania joins 47 African nations in Moscow summit
tz.dek: Prime Minister Mwigulu Nchemba represented Tanzania at the Third Summit of Heads of State and Government discussing economic cooperation and security.
paragraphs: Tanzania joined 47 other African nations in Moscow, Russia, for the Third Summit of Heads of State and Government. Prime Minister Dr Mwigulu Nchemba attended the opening ceremony, which Russian President Vladimir Putin officially opened on Wednesday. The summit focused on economic cooperation, security, science, technology, and social issues, with 22 heads of state present.

African leaders, including President Nchemba representing Tanzania, pressed Russia for investments that create jobs and process local resources. Burundi President Évariste Ndayishimiye, the African Union chairperson, stated that Africa sought to strengthen partner ties and wanted partnerships that turn resources into domestic production and higher-value exports. President Putin highlighted Russia's digital payment infrastructure as a tool to expand cross-border services.

The summit, themed 'Platform for Independent Development: Russia’s Advanced Solutions in Key Economic and Social Sectors', showcased Russia's capabilities in industry, agriculture, energy, transport, finance, digital technologies, healthcare, and education. Russia-Africa trade reportedly exceeded US$27 billion in 2025, and Russia supplied over 15 million tonnes of grain to the continent last year.

tz.headline: Tanzania marks one year since deadly election unrest
tz.dek: Official figures state 518 people died and over 2,000 were injured in the October 29, 2025 events.
paragraphs: One year after the October 29, 2025 election day violence, stakeholders gathered on October 29, 2026, to assess the nation's progress. Official figures report at least 518 people died and over 2,000 were injured during the events.

Human rights advocate Dr. Helen Kijo-Bisimba, civil society executive Lutgard Kokulinda Kagaruki, lawyer Jebra Kambole, and others participated in the Kivulini Talks session. The discussion, moderated by Khalifa Said, focused on what is known and unknown about the unrest, and the steps taken since.

President Samia Suluhu Hassan established two commissions following the events. While official figures cite around 500 deaths, unofficial reports suggest thousands were killed and injured, with significant property destruction.

tz.headline: Tanzania plans to cut state funding for public firms
tz.dek: A 25-year roadmap aims to make public corporations financially self-reliant, reducing dependence on government subsidies.
paragraphs: Tanzania is launching a 25-year plan to make its public institutions financially independent. The Office of the Treasury Registrar (OTR) will coordinate reforms to decrease reliance on government subsidies for public and statutory corporations (PSCs). Commercial entities are expected to fund their own operations, while those providing essential services will receive appropriate support.

President Samia Suluhu Hassan has urged public institutions to improve performance and reduce their need for routine government support, particularly those receiving subsidies without delivering results. Chief Secretary Ambassador Dr Moses Kusiluka stressed the need for better revenue collection and expenditure control. An analysis of 227 PSCs shows that government subventions are the primary financing source for most, with Treasury support increasing by an average of about 15 per cent annually over three financial years.

Nearly 82 per cent of these institutions depend on government financing, with fewer than one in five operating on a self-sustaining basis. The reform framework distinguishes between recurrent and development funding, acknowledging that investments in infrastructure like water treatment plants or transport may not generate immediate revenue. The goal is to encourage stronger management and cost efficiency.
