tz.headline: Tanzania accused of using laws to silence critics
tz.dek: Families of those killed in election violence demand justice and medical aid, while rights groups cite abuse of counterterrorism laws.
paragraphs: Families of at least 500 people killed in election-related violence a year ago are demanding justice and help with medical bills. Neema Munuo, whose 18-year-old daughter Maria Chami was shot dead on election day, wants the government to acknowledge her suffering. Meshack Sane, who was shot in the leg, told the BBC that families can no longer afford hospital expenses.

On the anniversary of President Samia Suluhu Hassan's election with 98% of the vote, Amnesty International accused her government of weaponising counterterrorism laws to silence critics and instill fear. The opposition dismissed the election result as a mockery of democracy, as two main challengers were excluded.

Tundu Lissu, the 58-year-old leader of the main opposition Chadema party, was put on trial for treason before the poll, preventing him from standing. A verdict in his case is due next week. Lissu had been demanding electoral reforms and recently went on a hunger strike, alleging denial of access to lawyers, which prison authorities denied.

ma.headline: Morocco raises income tax exemption threshold
ma.dek: Starting January 1, 2027, 87% of employees will pay no income tax, with potential monthly gains of MAD 500.
paragraphs: Morocco's 2027 Finance Bill proposes increasing the annual income tax exemption threshold from MAD 40,000 to MAD 60,000. Economy and Finance Minister Fouzi Lekjaa stated last Friday that this change, effective January 1, 2027, will exempt 87% of employees from income tax. The reform is projected to cost the state MAD 5.5 billion, with most affected employees gaining around MAD 500 monthly.

The new tax rates will see income between MAD 60,001 and MAD 80,000 taxed at 10%, MAD 80,001 to MAD 100,000 at 20%, MAD 100,001 to MAD 180,000 at 34%, and income above MAD 180,000 at 37%. Professional expense deductions will rise to 45%. Researcher Oussama Boughda noted that while employees are the primary beneficiaries, the changes also apply to professional and real estate income.

The reform will be phased in until 2031, when top tax rates will be 30%. Boughda estimated monthly gains could range from less than MAD 100 to MAD 500, depending on individual circumstances and family status. For instance, an employee earning MAD 10,000 monthly could see their net salary increase from MAD 8,904 to MAD 9,346.

ma.headline: Moroccan MPs question 2027 finance bill details
ma.dek: Lawmakers raise concerns over social aid, student grants, and electricity bill exemptions.
paragraphs: Moroccan MPs debated the 2027 Finance Bill on Thursday, with specific concerns raised about social aid and student grants. The House of Representatives’ Finance and Economic Development Committee heard calls to review eligibility criteria for financial support and ensure fairer public investment distribution.

PAM MP Imane Lamaoui highlighted limited university options in Ouarzazate, forcing students to incur extra costs. She welcomed a plan to increase grant recipients to 430,000 but argued that current income-based criteria exclude many needy students. RNI’s Taoufik Kamil questioned the government’s economic policy, noting that food prices have risen 29% since 2017, and criticized electricity bill exemptions that may miss poorer households.

Kamil also pointed out that despite increased health budgets, the sector’s problems persist. MPs stressed that student grants are an investment in Morocco’s future, warning that dropouts mean the country loses potential skilled workers. The debate also touched on advanced regionalization and the need for clear targets in human capital investment.

ma.headline: Morocco parties get November 15 deadline for election law changes
ma.dek: Interior Ministry seeks proposals for 2027 local, regional, and professional elections following parliamentary vote.
paragraphs: Morocco’s Interior Ministry has set November 15 as the deadline for political parties to submit proposed changes to electoral laws for the 2027 local, regional, and professional elections. This move follows September's parliamentary elections and initiates preparations for the next electoral cycle under royal instructions.

The deadline was announced after consultations on Thursday between the interior minister and party leaders, including those outside parliamentary groups. Discussions focused on extending measures from the September 23, 2026, elections, aimed at strengthening electoral integrity, to the upcoming contests for communal, provincial, and regional councils, professional chambers, and the House of Councillors.

Party representatives shared initial observations, with the ministry requesting written proposals to shape draft amendments. The government aims to complete legal preparations for the 2027 elections promptly. Participating parties expressed willingness to contribute to the process, which follows a September parliamentary election that reshaped the political landscape.

ug.headline: Uganda's EAC trade deficit hits $809 million
ug.dek: Imports from Kenya and Tanzania far outstripped Uganda's exports in August 2026, widening the regional trade gap.
paragraphs: Uganda's trade deficit with the East African Community (EAC) reached $809 million in August 2026, driven by a surge in imports from Kenya and Tanzania. The country earned $241.29 million from exports to the bloc but spent $1.05 billion on imports, creating a significant imbalance.

Kenya alone accounted for $714.5 million in Ugandan imports, with only $41.05 million in Ugandan exports to Kenya, resulting in a $673.45 million deficit. Tanzania contributed another $189.8 million deficit, with imports at $203.6 million against exports of $13.8 million.

These deficits with Kenya and Tanzania outweighed surpluses with the Democratic Republic of Congo ($77.1 million), South Sudan ($56.71 million), and Rwanda ($21.89 million). The Bank of Uganda linked this widening deficit to pressure on the Uganda shilling and concerns about imported inflation.

ug.headline: Museveni urges church to champion wealth creation
ug.dek: President Museveni's message at the 141st Bishop Hannington commemoration stressed combining spiritual guidance with practical efforts to improve livelihoods.
paragraphs: President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni has urged the Church of Uganda and other religious institutions to promote socio-economic transformation and household wealth creation. The President's message was delivered by Minister for the Presidency, Hon. Babirye Milly Babalanda, at the 141st commemoration of Bishop James Hannington in Mayuge District.

The commemoration honoured the Anglican missionary martyred in Uganda in 1885. President Museveni thanked the Church of Uganda, the organising committee, and the people of Busoga for keeping Bishop Hannington’s legacy alive, noting his faith, courage, and sacrifice. Bishop Hannington first led missionaries to Uganda in 1882, facing numerous challenges.

He returned in 1885 with fellow missionaries like William Jones, but they were detained near Lake Victoria as their motives were misunderstood by the Kabaka. Bishop Hannington was killed on October 29, 1885, on the orders of Kabaka Mwanga II, through Busoga Chief Luba, at Kyando.

ug.headline: Uganda screens over 30,000 buildings for earthquake safety
ug.dek: The National Building Review Board is updating seismic risk maps and construction standards to protect communities.
paragraphs: Uganda is assessing over 30,000 buildings nationwide to improve earthquake preparedness and construction safety. The National Building Review Board (NBRB) is conducting these assessments to identify structural weaknesses and guide necessary strengthening interventions. This work is part of the Serene initiative to update seismic risk mapping and improve building regulations.

Eng. Dr Maurice Oleng, head of research at the NBRB, stated that the building screenings provide evidence for revising construction standards and disaster preparedness plans. The NBRB is collaborating with the Global Earthquake Model Foundation on this project, which examines earthquake hazards, population exposure, and building vulnerability. Updated seismic hazard assessments now identify areas more susceptible to ground shaking, particularly around the East African Rift System.

Research also includes assessing 100 school buildings in Fort Portal, Hoima, and Mbarara for earthquake vulnerability, with findings expected to inform targeted improvements. The NBRB aims to update Uganda's seismic design code to ensure engineers have a foundational baseline for constructing resilient structures. These efforts follow a recent church collapse in Bwerenga that killed one person and injured 25, where preliminary assessments cited design weaknesses and poor workmanship.

ug.headline: Uganda: epilepsy drug mix-up kills child, hospitalises 16
ug.dek: Health workers in Butebo district administered carbamazepine instead of deworming medicine during a child outreach.
paragraphs: A two-year-old boy died and 16 children were hospitalised in Butebo district after health workers mistakenly gave them an epilepsy drug instead of deworming medicine. The incident occurred during a child health outreach in Kabwangasi town council on October 30, 2026. The children were given carbamazepine, an epilepsy drug, instead of mebendazole, a deworming medicine, reportedly because the tablets looked similar.

The affected children were rushed to Mbale Regional Referral Hospital, where they developed severe central nervous system depression. Dr Julian Abeso stated that one child died from respiratory depression, while 15 others began recovering from deep sedation. The hospital notified the ministry of Health, and the health workers involved have been suspended pending investigation.

Butebo district health officer Dr Lawrence Oowunye confirmed 23 children received the wrong medication, with 17 showing severe symptoms. The district has suspended all community health outreaches to audit its medicine supply systems. Police and the National Drug Authority are investigating how the mix-up occurred at both packing and administration stages.

ug.dek: The online marketplace offers discounts on electronics, appliances, and fashion from October 30 to November 30.
paragraphs: Jumia Uganda has launched its annual Black Friday shopping campaign, offering discounts of up to 80% on selected items. cv.headline: Emileno Ortet launches grogue brand DeePuna for export
cv.dek: Cape Verdean entrepreneur Emileno Ortet aims to sell his grogue and ponche to the US and Europe.
paragraphs: Emileno Ortet, from São Domingos, has created DeePuna, a brand of grogue and ponche named after his mother, with ambitions for international markets. Ortet, who grew up in a family involved in commerce, saw the economic potential of grogue and developed this entrepreneurial project. He previously emigrated to the United States in search of better opportunities, where he identified a business opening for his native product.

After two years of preparation, including cultivating sugarcane, refining production, and obtaining export licenses, DeePuna has been launched in Praia and is available domestically. The primary goal remains internationalisation, with the US as the first target market due to Ortet's familiarity and existing contacts there. He is also seeking partnerships in Europe to expand the brand.

Ortet believes the Cape Verdean aguardente holds significant promise in the US and European markets, particularly among the diaspora who appreciate the flavours of home. He is confident that both grogue and ponche will find a receptive audience abroad, driven by a sense of nostalgia for their homeland's tastes.

The meeting also covered South-South cooperation based on expertise sharing and African solidarity for the continent's energy sovereignty. The Tanzanian delegation's program included meetings with aeronautical and port authorities, a ship visit, and presentations on carbon governance and registration.

Digital content was seized during the operations.

The suspects have been transferred to the Public Prosecutor following the completion of investigations. This action is part of a broader awareness campaign against online abuses launched by the cybersecurity agency.

The announcement comes less than a month after a similar arrest on October 7 for online child sexual abuse. Authorities have recently increased calls for public vigilance against offenses committed on social networks.

sz.headline: Court stops Eswatini National Provident Fund board inauguration
sz.dek: Business and labour federations challenged the appointment process, leading to an interim court order.
paragraphs: The High Court has issued an interim order stopping the inauguration and public announcement of the newly formed Eswatini National Provident Fund (ENPF) Board. Labour and Social Security Minister Phila Buthelezi had announced the Board at SibaneSami Hotel just a day before the court order. The halt follows an urgent application by business and labour groups contesting the selection process.

The application, filed by the Federation of Eswatini Business Community (FESBEC), Business Eswatini, and the Trade Union Congress of Swaziland (TUCOSWA), challenges the exclusion of two nominees and the appointment of Ministry of Labour Principal Secretary Makhosini Mndawe. Applicants argue that decisions to exclude FESBEC nominee Themba Dlamini and Business Eswatini nominee E. Nathi Dlamini, and to appoint Mndawe, were irregular and violated representation arrangements.

Applicants stated that an ordinary court process could take approximately three months, and allowing disputed appointments to stand could prejudice their interests. They received electronic notification on Tuesday evening, October 27, 2026, for an inauguration the following morning, leaving insufficient time for a standard review before the event.

sz.headline: Police allege PUDEMO president coordinated 2021 unrest by phone
sz.dek: Mlungisi Makhanya and Zweli Martin Dlamini allegedly directed ground activities and received stolen firearms during the 2021-2023 unrest, according to court papers.
paragraphs: Eswatini police allege that Mlungisi Makhanya, president of the proscribed People’s United Democratic Movement (PUDEMO), and Swaziland News Editor Zweli Martin Dlamini coordinated the 2021/22 unrest via phone calls. Assistant Superintendent Bhekani Shiba stated in court papers that stolen firearms were surrendered to Makhanya. These allegations are part of an application for the extradition of Ntokozo Kenneth Vilakati, also known as ‘Putin’, who is reportedly arrested in South Africa.

Shiba, the investigating officer, claims Makhanya and Dlamini gave instructions to individuals on the ground, linking them to the activities of a group called the ‘underground solidarity forces’. The investigator alleges Vilakati acted on orders from this group’s commander, Thabo Kunene, and others, including Makhanya. The police account connects the group to alleged offences across Eswatini’s four regions between 2021 and 2023.

The court papers detail alleged operations involving Vilakati, including incidents at Dumako, the homestead of the late Chief Justice Bheki Maphalala, and properties near Pigg’s Peak. These include alleged cattle killings, house burnings, and the burning of a truck and forest belonging to Rockland Company. The Central Transport Administration block and Pigg’s Peak Magistrates Court were allegedly burnt the following morning.

sz.headline: Eswatini attracts E1.85 billion in new investments
sz.dek: The Eswatini Investment Promotion Authority facilitated projects expected to create 147 jobs.
paragraphs: Eswatini attracted E1.85 billion in new investment projects and E170 million in expansion projects during the second quarter of the 2026/27 financial year. These projects are expected to support 147 jobs once at full capacity. The Eswatini Investment Promotion Authority (EIPA) facilitated these investments, according to the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Trade’s Second Quarter Performance Report.

The report, covering July to September 2026, was presented under Minister Manqoba Khumalo. EIPA also conducted five outward investment promotion missions to Zimbabwe, South Africa, and Zambia. Cumulative potential export orders increased to E3 million, and the authority supported six additional exporters.

EIPA launched the buyeswatini.shop platform, which onboarded 29 sellers and recorded 40 transactions. The Mavuso Trade and Exhibition Centre website and digital booking platform were also completed. The Registrar of Companies registered 790 companies, including 637 Emaswati-owned businesses.

sz.headline: Mbabane derby to decide Charity Cup
sz.dek: Mbabane Highlanders and Mbabane Swallows will clash in the PLE Charity Cup final on November 8.
paragraphs: Mbabane Highlanders will face Mbabane Swallows in the Premier League of Eswatini (PLE) Charity Cup final on November 8 at Mavuso Sports Centre. The derby match will kick off at 4:15pm, following an earlier game between Green Mamba and Ubombo Sugar. The winners of the elite league tournament will receive E1 million.

Under businesswoman Shauwn ‘MaMkhize’ Mkhize, Highlanders aim to extend their winning streak against Swallows, having beaten them 4-0 and 1-0 in previous matches. The PLE secured E1.5 million in sponsorship for the Charity Cup, which returns after being last staged in 2019. Highlanders won that tournament, defeating Manzini Wanderers 3-1.

The play-offs for the tournament are scheduled for November 1, with semi-finals and the final on November 8. These dates were moved from September 27 and October 4 to accommodate FIFA fixtures. The National First Division will also have a final on finals day with E200 000 for the competition. Proceeds from the event will support non-governmental organisations.

ga.headline: Gabon navy finds three bodies in Prospector 5 wreck
ga.dek: Two people remain missing after the Prospector 5 vessel sank, with recovery operations underway.
paragraphs: Gabon's navy located three bodies inside the sunken Prospector 5 shipwreck on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. The discovery occurred four days after the vessel sank, with two individuals still unaccounted for. Underwater inspections using a remote-operated vehicle (ROV) led to the finding of the bodies within the submerged wreck.

Vice-Admiral Charles Hubert Bekale-Meyong, Chief of Staff of the National Navy, announced the discovery. Identification of the bodies is pending further examination. Recovery operations are being prepared by technical teams with specialized personnel. A total of 110 people have been rescued since the shipwreck, with naval, air, and oil company resources mobilized.

An investigation into the circumstances of the disaster was opened on October 25, 2026, by the prosecutor of the Tchibanga Court of First Instance. The priority remains the recovery and identification of the three bodies and the continued search for the two missing persons. BW Energy Gabon SA is jointly conducting operations with the rescue command.

ga.headline: Gabon votes to lift US embargo on Cuba
ga.dek: The UN General Assembly passed a resolution calling for the end of the US embargo on Cuba, with Gabon supporting the measure.
paragraphs: Gabon voted on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, at the United Nations General Assembly in New York to support the resolution demanding the lifting of the United States embargo against Cuba. This vote occurred amidst international tensions between Washington and Havana, with the resolution adopted by 130 votes in favour, 17 against, and 25 abstentions.

The resolution, presented by Cuba, urges other countries not to apply similar measures and denounces the extraterritorial effects of the 1996 Helms-Burton Act. This diplomatic action comes as Cuba faces severe economic and energy shortages, with electricity outages impacting essential services like transport, water distribution, and hospitals.

The vote reflects a declining international support for the resolution compared to previous years, with 165 votes in favour in 2025 and 187 in 2024. The US ambassador to the UN contested the existence of a blockade, while Havana accused Washington of economic strangulation. The adopted resolution remains non-binding.

ga.headline: World Bank reviews Gabon's public finances
ga.dek: The financial institution presented its 2026 economic outlook to the CESEC on October 28, 2026.
paragraphs: The World Bank presented its 2026 economic outlook for Gabon on October 28, 2026, to officials and advisors of the Economic, Social, Environmental and Cultural Council (CESEC). The report details the country's public finances and economic prospects, highlighting the challenge of translating analysis into concrete reforms for diversified, productive, and job-creating growth.

Sylvain Kakou, the World Bank's resident representative, led the delegation that reviewed Gabon's public finances with CESEC members. This meeting renews the cooperation framework between Gabon and the World Bank, aligning with the Gabonese authorities' ambition to structurally transform the national economy as outlined in the 2026-2030 National Growth and Development Plan.

The review focused on six areas: the macroeconomic and budgetary context, public revenues, the quality and efficiency of state spending, and public finance management. It also examined revenues from extractive sectors like oil, mines, and forests, alongside public investment management, budgets, treasury, and debt, including social spending on education, health, and social protection.

ga.headline: Gabon hosts Congo Basin civil society for COP31 talks
ga.dek: Over 50 participants from six countries met in Libreville to forge a common stance on climate finance and local rights.
paragraphs: Libreville, Gabon, became the center for green diplomacy in the Congo Basin on October 28, 2026, as over 50 participants from six countries gathered for a two-day conference. Environmental civil society organizations from Cameroon, Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Central African Republic, Democratic Republic of Congo, and Gabon convened to build a unified position before COP31.

The conference, themed "A resilient Congo Basin: forests, populations, finances and nature," aims to ensure the region, the planet's second-largest green lung, arrives at COP31 united and coordinated. Key discussions focused on the role of local communities and indigenous peoples, with participants demanding effective decision-making participation and direct access to climate finance. Indigenous peoples presented nine demands, including formal recognition of their rights and reduced extractive industries on their territories.

Martial Dinang, executive secretary of Brainforest, emphasized that forest preservation should not compromise the rights of local populations, stressing the need to protect livelihoods and ensure their effective participation in decisions. Etienne Dourani Toko, representing local communities in Gabon, stated that nature cannot be preserved by marginalizing its guardians. Only 2.1% of climate funds reportedly reach forest guardians.

ga.headline: Gabon police arrest three over failed explosive bank heist
ga.dek: Suspects accused of attempting to blow up a vehicle carrying Olam employee payroll funds near Bitam.
paragraphs: Three individuals have been arrested and detained in Gabon for allegedly attempting to rob a vehicle carrying payroll funds for Olam employees. The suspects are accused of using explosives in the failed heist on September 6, 2026, on the Bitam-Mongomo road in the Woleu-Ntem province.

The targeted vehicle belonged to Sodec, a subsidiary, and was transporting funds for Olam-Batouri workers. The attackers reportedly planted an industrial explosive device the day before. The blast damaged the vehicle, which carried seven bank agents and one armed gendarme, but no one was injured.

The suspects were apprehended by the Directorate General of Research (DGR) and the Bitam mobile gendarmerie unit. They face charges of attempted armed robbery with explosives and criminal association, and have been placed in pre-trial detention in Bitam.

gm.headline: Gambia begins repaying D563.8 million bus loan
gm.dek: The government made its first principal and interest payment in May 2026 for buses procured for the Gambia Transport Service Company.
paragraphs: The Gambian government has started repaying a D563.8 million loan for buses acquired by the Gambia Transport Service Company (GTSC). The first payment covering principal and interest was made in May 2026, according to Finance Minister Seedy Keita.

Minister Keita informed the National Assembly that the D563,779,771.50 financing will be repaid over 10 semi-annual instalments. The repayment schedule began on April 30, 2026, and is scheduled to conclude by October 30, 2030.

The loan was provided by the Social Security and Housing Finance Corporation (SSHFC) to fund the purchase of GTSC buses. The government is expected to continue these bi-annual payments until the loan is fully settled.

gm.headline: Gambia develops clean cooking strategy
gm.dek: The initiative, supported by the EU and Netherlands, aims to promote safer, cleaner cooking solutions across the nation.
paragraphs: Gambia is creating a National Clean Cooking Strategy to promote safer and more sustainable cooking methods. This effort is part of the Regional Clean Cooking Action in West Africa (ReCCAWA) programme, which supports clean cooking technologies in 12 West African nations. A national workshop was held on Wednesday at the Sir Dawda Kairaba Jawara International Conference Centre to discuss the strategy's development.

The programme, funded by the European Union and the Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs through ECOWAS, targets demand, supply, and policy for clean cooking. Carmen, representing the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO), stated that clean cooking is vital for the health of women and children, environmental protection, and business growth. She highlighted that women and children suffer from toxic smoke and that firewood use pressures forests.

The Deputy Head of the EU Delegation to The Gambia, Raphaël Brigandi, linked clean cooking to environmental protection, women's empowerment, and private sector development. He expressed hope that the workshop would lead to a strong national strategy guiding future policies and actions. The strategy aims to improve health, protect the environment, empower women, and create business opportunities.

gm.headline: Gambia launches hub for 20 returning migrants
gm.dek: Kanifing Municipal Council offers services and business support to help returnees rebuild lives.
paragraphs: The Kanifing Municipal Council (KMC) launched the Kanifing Migrant Resilience Hub on October 29, 2026, to support 20 returning migrants. The initiative, backed by the Mayors Migration Council's Global Cities Fund 2025, aims to help returnees rebuild their lives and reintegrate sustainably. Lord Mayor Talib Ahmed Bensouda led the launch, emphasizing the council's commitment to inclusive development.

Mayor Bensouda stated the hub addresses the reality of young people leaving Gambia due to perceived lack of opportunity. He praised the courage of those who returned and are now seeking to restart their lives. The Hub will connect participants with services, resources, and opportunities to strengthen their livelihoods and confidence. Businesses supported include waste collection, delivery services, tailoring, and car painting.

The Resilience Hub includes a childcare centre and psychosocial support services to allow participants to focus on their enterprises. KMC aims to foster collaboration with entities like Startup Incubator Gambia to create lasting opportunities. The council seeks to make Kanifing a place where young people can succeed locally by starting businesses and creating jobs.

gm.headline: Gambia reaffirms UN Charter principles
gm.dek: Vice President Jallow called for stronger partnerships to advance global peace and human rights at UN Day.
paragraphs: Vice President Mohammed B.S. Jallow stated on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, that The Gambia remains committed to the UN Charter's principles. Speaking at the 81st United Nations Day celebration in Bijilo, he emphasized the need for international cooperation to tackle global challenges.

The event, themed “Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations That Delivers for All,” saw VP Jallow commend the UN Country Team for supporting The Gambia’s National Development Plan, ‘YIRIWA’ 2023–2027. He stressed that restoring trust requires transparency and accountability for tangible improvements in people’s lives.

UN Resident Coordinator Karl Frédérick Paul noted that while trust is tested globally, commitment to multilateralism should not waver. He referenced conflicts in Sudan, Gaza, and Ukraine, where civilians suffer from peace failures and climate disruption.

gn.headline: Guinea hosts francophone telecom regulators
gn.dek: Conakry meeting addresses digital infrastructure deployment and connectivity challenges.
paragraphs: Conakry, Guinea, hosted the 24th annual meeting of the Francophone Network of Telecommunications Regulation (FRATEL) starting October 29, 2026. The conference, preceded by an ITU workshop, gathered regulators and experts to discuss measures for deploying digital infrastructure. The goal is to harmonize regulatory and economic tools for effective, accessible, and resilient networks across the francophone space.

Mamady Doumbouya, Director General of Guinea's Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (ARPT), highlighted progress since the ACE fiber optic cable arrived 12 years ago. Guinea now has 13 million mobile subscribers, connecting three in four citizens, and nearly 12 million people to mobile internet, or two in three. However, over 600 localities in Guinea still lack network coverage.

To address these gaps, Doumbouya outlined a three-pillar strategy: sharing infrastructure like pylons and fiber to reduce costs, extending coverage to over 600 villages, and ensuring user trust through network quality control and market data publication. The ARPT aims to gather proposals during the two-day meeting.

paragraphs: AS Kalombada defeated Alu Star 1-0 in a Ligue 2 match on Thursday, October 29, 2026, at the Yorokoguia stadium. Kabiné Sakho scored the winning goal in the 90th+3 minute, securing a late victory for the Siguiri club.

The match, part of the 9th round of the Ligue 2 championship, was tense with few clear chances in the first half, ending 0-0. AS Kalombada intensified their pressure after halftime, and Sakho's goal came during a moment of confusion in the Alu Star defense.

gw.headline: Guinea-Bissau minister urges realistic budgets
gw.dek: Communication Minister Abduramane Turé called for financial capacity assessment before state commitments.
paragraphs: Guinea-Bissau's Minister of Social Communication, Abduramane Turé, on Thursday, October 29, 2026, advocated for a strict evaluation of financial execution capacity before the state takes on new commitments. Speaking at the opening of the INACEP Activity Planning Retreat for 2027, Turé stated that planning must be based on clear priorities, realistic objectives, and resources aligned with the institution's financial capacity.

The two-day retreat, themed “Planning for the repositioning of INACEP as the State's national documentary security service,” aims to define the activity plan and budget for the upcoming year. Minister Turé emphasized that an effective plan requires a realistic diagnosis, identification of challenges, establishment of priorities, and measurable indicators. He highlighted technological modernization, digital transformation, operational capacity strengthening, and human resource development as priority areas.

Lemes Monteiro, the Director-General of INACEP, announced that the retreat will conclude with the development of the 2027 activity plan and budget. He acknowledged the institution's challenges, pointing to the regularization of retiring staff through social security as a priority. The minister urged the adoption of concrete solutions for identified problems, advocating for a financially sustainable and feasible planning document.

gw.headline: Firkidja di Pubis denounces regime crisis
gw.dek: Political movement calls for international sanctions against coup leaders and return to democracy.
paragraphs: The political movement Firkidja di Pubis denounced on Thursday, October 29, 2026, an alleged internal crisis within Guinea-Bissau's current regime. The group called on the international community to impose sanctions on those responsible for blocking the political process and demanded a return to democratic order and the release of political prisoners.

In a statement, Firkidja di Pubis described the situation as a "palace coup" within the regime that emerged from the November 2025 coup. They cited the disarmament of militias loyal to former President Umaro Sissoco Embaló, his prevented return to the country, changes in the Ministry of Interior, the Court of Accounts, and the Prosecutor General's Office, as well as military hierarchy adjustments, as evidence of internal disputes.

The movement stated that the division within the ruling bloc stems from a lack of political cohesion, disagreements over the election calendar, power struggles, and the pursuit of external support. Firkidja di Pubis also called for justice and transparency in managing the crisis and reiterated its opposition to the military high command remaining in power.

lr.headline: US investors eye Liberia's mining and energy sectors
lr.dek: American companies are exploring long-term investment in Liberia's mineral resources and energy infrastructure.
paragraphs: The United States has observed growing interest from American companies in Liberia's mining and energy sectors, with several businesses exploring long-term investment opportunities. U.S. Chargé d’Affaires Kristin Gilmore stated on Wednesday, October 28, that multiple private-sector delegations have visited Liberia recently, indicating significant commercial interest in the country's mineral wealth and energy potential.

Gilmore explained that Liberia's drive to attract foreign investment and develop its mining and energy sectors aligns with U.S. goals to diversify global supply chains. The Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) confirmed Liberia's eligibility for a second compact focused on mining and electricity reforms to spur private investment. The U.S. Trade and Development Agency is also finalizing a grant to assess Liberia’s railway infrastructure for a multi-user system.

Attracting sustained foreign investment requires transparent regulations, predictable policies, reliable electricity, and fair infrastructure access, Gilmore noted, citing that developing a new mine averages 18 years. American companies can offer technical expertise, workforce training, technology transfer, and investment, while expanding local supply chains and creating jobs.

The project, estimated to cost between US$261 million and US$506 million over 10 years, aims to start with a national high-performance wheelchair basketball center and expand into an international sports destination.

This initiative seeks to reduce barriers such as limited access to specialized facilities, equipment, and training for athletes living with disabilities. The proposed village would offer accessible sports facilities, specialized coaching, sports medicine, and technical support, potentially creating employment and attracting international partnerships.

The proposal aligns with the Liberian government's ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development (AAID), which prioritizes inclusion and opportunities for persons with disabilities. While the ambition is significant, the project faces a major hurdle in securing funding, with feasibility studies and detailed designs still required.

lr.headline: Liberia Water Justice Forum launched to demand safe water access
lr.dek: A new advocacy group calls on the Liberian government to ensure equitable and affordable provision of safe drinking water for all citizens.
paragraphs: A new water advocacy group, the Liberia Water Justice Forum, was launched in Brewerville, outside Monrovia. The Forum, a collaboration between Church Aid International (CAI), the Fellowship of Christian Councils and Churches in West Africa (FECCIWA), and the Africa Water Justice Network, aims to advocate for access to safe drinking water across Liberia.

CAI Chairman Bishop Kortu Brown stated that the Forum will ask difficult questions about water access and hold leaders accountable. He emphasized that leaders must be prepared to answer these questions to address societal challenges, particularly concerning the provision of accessible and affordable safe drinking water for all Liberians, especially women and children.

The group also called on concession companies operating in Liberia to pay fees for allegedly polluting rivers and creeks. Rev. Christopher Toe, Secretary General of the Liberia Council of Churches, noted that the Forum's launch aligns with pillar six of the Sustainable Development Goals, which focuses on clean water and sanitation.

lr.headline: Liberia's NaFAA secures US$325,000 FAO grant
lr.dek: The funds will support a new fish sales hub in Congo Town, Monrovia, with a cooling room and training.
paragraphs: The National Fisheries & Aquaculture Authority (NaFAA) in Liberia has received a US$325,000 grant from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO). The grant, under the Technical Cooperation Programme, will fund the construction of an improved Fish Sales Hub in Congo Town, Monrovia.

The planned facility will include a 20-tonne cooling room, waste management systems, specialized delivery motorbikes, and smart-energy features. It will also provide training for fishmongers and include a small seafood grill. The initiative aims to improve market access for local fish producers and reduce post-harvest losses.

The grant will also assist the University of Liberia's Department of Fisheries and Aquaculture Sciences in developing a Small-Scale Fisheries Guideline, curriculum, and training materials. The Fish Sales Hub is intended to operate as a Public–Private Partnership.

lr.headline: Liberia Baptist Seminary opens conference on drug addiction
lr.dek: The Liberia Baptist Theological Seminary conference addresses drug addiction, recovery, and youth empowerment.
paragraphs: The Liberia Baptist Theological Seminary (LBTS) opened its Fifth International Theological Education Conference (ITEC) in Paynesville, Liberia, on October 30, 2026. LBTS President Rev. Dr. Prof. Momolu A. Massaquoi warned that Liberia’s future generation is at risk from drug addiction if the crisis is not urgently addressed.

The two-day conference, themed “Healing the Next Generation: The Theological Perspective on Drug Addiction, Recovery, and Youth Empowerment,” began at the Bradley D. and Carolyn Brown Fellowship Chapel. Keynote speaker Rev. Dr. Stephen L. Hawkins urged religious leaders to view addiction not just as a personal character failure but as a complex issue influenced by social and economic factors.

Hawkins, a sociologist of religion, highlighted hope, human dignity, and reintegration as guiding principles for addiction discussions. He cited examples from the United States, including New Brunswick, New Jersey, and New Orleans, Louisiana, to illustrate how poverty, mental health, and limited opportunities can contribute to substance abuse among young people.

ly.headline: Libyan dialogue group seeks judicial unity for elections
ly.dek: London talks focus on resolving institutional divisions to enable credible presidential and parliamentary votes.
paragraphs: Libya's UN-facilitated 4+4 dialogue group met in London and agreed to consult more widely with the judiciary to resolve institutional divisions. Participants stated these divisions threaten the prospects for credible national elections.

The group, meeting under UN Special Representative Hanna Tetteh, identified judicial unity and independence as essential for holding presidential and parliamentary votes that would be accepted across political divides. Members committed to seeking political support for the electoral agreement signed in Tripoli on August 30 and will meet again in two weeks.

The August agreement addresses reconstituting the High National Elections Commission board and settling disputes over the constitutional and legal framework for polls. It envisages elections under a single executive authority within 24 months, though this remains a political commitment. The High Council of State has rejected the agreement, citing concerns about bypassing established rules.

ly.headline: Libyan professor links wage reform to spending control
ly.dek: Ali Al-Sharif stated that managing oil revenues transparently is key to closing wage gaps.
paragraphs: An economics professor from the University of Benghazi, Ali Al-Sharif, stated that reforming Libya's salaries requires controlling public spending and improving the governance of oil revenues. Al-Sharif told Al-Araby Al-Jadeed newspaper that rationalizing expenses and ensuring transparent collection and management of oil money are necessary steps. He said these measures are needed to close wage gaps in a sustainable manner.

Al-Sharif, who teaches at the University of Benghazi, emphasized the need for transparency in how oil revenues are managed. He indicated that controlling spending is a prerequisite for any successful wage reform. The professor's comments were made in an interview with Al-Araby Al-Jadeed newspaper.

The professor's remarks focus on the financial and governance aspects of salary imbalances. He did not provide specific figures for wage gaps or spending targets. The next step would involve the government implementing policies based on such economic advice.

ly.headline: France warns citizens against travel to most of Libya
ly.dek: French authorities advise against travel to Tripoli due to volatile security, armed clashes, and crime risks.
paragraphs: French authorities have issued a travel advisory against visiting most of Libya, including the capital, Tripoli. Travel to Misrata, Sirte, and Benghazi is only recommended for absolutely essential purposes.

The updated French travel guidance highlights volatile security conditions, ongoing armed clashes, and a high risk of kidnapping and general crime. French citizens in Libya are urged to adopt strict security measures.
Consular services for French citizens in Libya will continue to be managed from Tunisia, even though the French Embassy in Tripoli reopened on March 29.

ly.headline: LAICO approves changes to protect overseas assets
ly.dek: Libyan African Investment Company's general assembly reviewed business plans and adopted new regulations on October 29.
paragraphs: The Libyan African Investment Company (LAICO) approved changes to its structure and regulations on Thursday, October 29, to safeguard overseas assets. The general assembly met at the Libya Africa Investment Portfolio’s (LAIP) headquarters in Tripoli to review LAICO’s business plan and future strategy.

LAICO members adopted a revised organisational structure and amendments to administrative, financial, and investment regulations. They also ratified financial statements for 2014–2020 and reviewed those for 2021–2025, endorsing an external audit firm and its fees.

The assembly assessed progress on resolutions from 2019 and 2021 meetings. LAICO’s business plan was considered within LAIP’s objectives to improve management efficiency and support sustained financial performance.

mg.headline: Madagascar seeks Russian investment in energy and agriculture
mg.dek: President Randrianirina wants Russian firms to process raw materials locally, creating jobs and industrial activity.
paragraphs: Madagascar's President, Colonel Michaël Randrianirina, attended the 3rd Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, outlining economic priorities and seeking stronger ties with Russia. He stated that despite destabilization attempts, Madagascar is committed to developing this partnership. The President highlighted the Madagascar-Russia Chamber of Commerce as a tool to connect investors.

Key sectors for new partnerships include energy, agriculture, health, water supply, digital technology, and scientific research. President Randrianirina aims to attract Russian companies willing to process raw materials directly in Madagascar, boosting local employment, tax revenue, and industrial development. Russia presented its A7 cross-border payment system, which has expanded in Africa.

The effectiveness of this summit will be measured by tangible benefits for the population, including mobilized funding, established businesses, created jobs, and completed infrastructure projects. The A7 payment platform, launched in late 2024, is expanding into Africa with existing offices in Nigeria and Zimbabwe.

mg.headline: Madagascar and Turkey seek more economic cooperation
mg.dek: Ankara is interested in increased collaboration in energy, education, and trade, with agriculture and mining also targeted.
paragraphs: Madagascar and Turkey aim to expand their economic partnership to attract more investments and development projects. This goal was stated on Thursday, October 29, in Antananarivo during a reception celebrating the 103rd anniversary of the Turkish Republic. Prime Minister Mamitiana Rajaonarison and several government officials attended the event.

Discussions focused on opportunities within Madagascar's economy, with the Minister of Public Security, Erick Michel Wouli Soumah Idrissa, expressing a desire to deepen bilateral ties. Ambassador Halime Ebru Demircan confirmed Turkey's interest in sectors like energy, education, and trade, highlighting the $80 million Ambohimanambola thermal power plant as a key achievement.

Future collaboration could extend to agriculture, infrastructure, mining, tourism, health, and renewable energy, supporting industrialization and job creation. Several agreements on fishing, electricity, and investment promotion are under discussion, with 181 Malagasy students having received Turkish university scholarships since 1992.

mg.headline: Madagascar pledges to centre women in ocean conservation
mg.dek: The island nation joins Belize in a global initiative to integrate female leadership into marine strategies and blue economies.
paragraphs: Madagascar has pledged to integrate women's leadership into national marine conservation strategies and blue economies. This commitment was made at the UN Biodiversity Conference (CoP17) as part of the Women Ocean Guardians Initiative. The global public-private partnership aims to place women at the forefront of ocean conservation and the sustainable use of marine resources.

Andrianirina Harinaivo Fanomezantsoa, Madagascar’s Coordonnateur Général, stated that women in Madagascar are vital team players in marine conservation and coastal community development. They serve in roles such as rangers, saving group leaders, park managers, and technical department leads. Madagascar joins 14 other governments that have made similar pledges.

The Women Ocean Guardians Initiative seeks to address gaps in the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, particularly Target 23 on gender equality, which remains the least advanced global goal. Management effectiveness and inclusive governance are identified as primary challenges for achieving the 30x30 ocean protection goal.

In preparation for the rainy season, the Agency for Public Investment Projects (Apipa) cleared debris and trash from the Andriantany canal in Ampefiloha to ensure water flow. This cleaning operation is ongoing in other locations.

mw.headline: Malawi NGOs earned K1.3 trillion in 2026
mw.dek: Non-governmental organisations in Malawi generated K1.30 trillion in income in 2026, with foreign currency making up 76.7 percent of this amount.
paragraphs: Non-governmental organisations (NGOs) in Malawi generated K1.30 trillion in income in 2026, an increase from K1.02 trillion in 2025, according to the 2026 NGO Sector Report. Foreign currency accounted for K994.6 billion, or 76.7 percent, of this total income. The report also noted that the top 20 NGOs received half of the total income generated.

Despite the income surge, paid employment within NGOs dropped to 22,440 in 2026 from 28,680 in 2025, though salaries totalled K337.2 billion. NGO Regulatory Authority (Ngora) CEO Voice Mhone stated that this income is a massive injection into the economy, almost rivaling the national budget. Minister of Gender, Children, Disability and Social Welfare Mary Navicha highlighted that nearly 39 percent of women are employed by NGOs.

Bertha Phiri, Ngora Board Chairperson, reported that NGO compliance levels are around 70 percent and that the sector has overtaken tobacco in foreign exchange earnings. The report, introduced by Ngora in 2021, consolidates financial and compliance records annually. Minister Navicha acknowledged the drop in employment but pledged continued government support to strengthen NGO systems and ensure transparent fund usage.

mw.headline: Malawi reforms fail to survive government changes
mw.dek: Eliya Zulu of Afidep says policy decisions are driven by short-term political interests, undermining development.
paragraphs: Economic reforms in Malawi are failing to survive government changes, according to Eliya Zulu, executive director of the African Institute for Development Policy (Afidep). Speaking at the Economics Association of Malawi (Ecama) 2026 Annual Economic Conference in Mangochi, Zulu stated that the lack of reform continuity weakens institutional memory and hinders long-term development.

Zulu noted that Malawi struggles economically despite having sound development strategies and qualified public servants, attributing this to policy decisions driven by short-term political interests and frequent changes in senior officials. Patrick Kabambe, Principal Secretary for Economic Planning and Development, also acknowledged institutional weaknesses affecting implementation.

The World Bank presented a mixed rating, stating that while Malawi shows signs of economic recovery with easing inflation, gains remain fragile and growth is projected to lag behind the sub-Saharan African average due to persistent macroeconomic challenges and external pressures.

mw.headline: Malawi farmers harvest more maize with WFP support
mw.dek: Levison Kamleka increased his maize yield from four to 21 bags after receiving anticipatory action intervention.
paragraphs: Levison Kamleka, a 45-year-old farmer in Zomba District, harvested 21 bags of maize in the 2025–2026 season, a significant increase from his usual three to four bags. This improvement followed support from the World Food Programme (WFP) through an anticipatory action intervention. Kamleka has used six bags for food and has 14 remaining, stating his days of seeking maize for food are over.

Kamleka's experience is part of WFP Malawi’s Zero Hunger Village (ZHV) model, launched in September 2025 and targeting 1,200 villages and 54,400 beneficiaries. The model integrates agricultural support, irrigation, school meals, nutrition services, climate information, and anticipatory action to combat hunger. In Nsanje District, irrigation support is enabling farmers like Chrissy Edward, 35, to grow crops despite unreliable rainfall.

Edward, from Bithi 1 Village, increased her rice harvest from two to three bags to nine bags from a 0.1-hectare plot using irrigation from the Shire River. Aline Bingara, 52, also in Nsanje, uses irrigation to grow sweet potatoes, maize, rice, and vegetables, enabling her to feed her family and sell surplus produce. The ZHV model aims to improve food availability, household incomes, children’s health, and school attendance.

mw.dek: The company aims to save foreign exchange and cut fossil fuel emissions with its new e-mobility system.
paragraphs: Sky Energy Africa is introducing 100 electric taxis and 40 fast chargers across Malawi, creating about 300 jobs. The sustainable energy enterprise, founded by Schizzo Thomson, is launching this e-mobility ecosystem to mark its tenth year in the country. A full charge for an electric vehicle (EV) covering 400 kilometres costs about K5 000 in electricity, while rapid charging sites will cost K25 000 for the same distance.

Thomson stated that after three years of learning, e-mobility is seen as the future solution for forex and fuel shortages, noting Malawi imports fuel worth $60 million monthly. Sky Energy, Malawi's premier EV dealer since 2023, developed the Sky e-Ride smart app, similar to Uber, allowing users to hail an e-taxi for as low as K1000 per kilometre. The company expects the 100 Geely EX2 electric taxis to transport approximately 5 500 people daily in Lilongwe, Mzuzu, and Blantyre.

Malawi Energy Regulatory Authority (Mera) spokesperson Fitina Khonje indicated that the country is collaborating with neighbours on EV regulations and aims to integrate EV chargers into existing fuel stations. The Ministry of Energy plans to launch the National E-Mobility Framework next Wednesday, with spokesperson Joan Thaundi expressing pleasure at the private sector's leading role in achieving e-mobility goals.

ml.headline: Malian higher education paralysed by strike
ml.dek: Teachers demand a research bonus promised nearly a decade ago, halting classes nationwide.
paragraphs: Higher education institutions across Mali are paralyzed by a strike of teacher-researchers. The industrial action began on October 26 and is scheduled to continue until the end of this week. The national union for the sector, CEN-SNESUP, called the strike.

CEN-SNESUP is demanding the payment of a research bonus that was promised almost 10 years ago but has never been disbursed. This has led to the complete shutdown of academic activities in universities and other higher learning facilities.

The strike affects students and faculty in all higher education institutions throughout Mali. The union's action highlights a long-standing grievance regarding unfulfilled financial promises to academic staff.

ml.headline: Bamako families fear for missing relatives amid rising murders
ml.dek: Police investigate three murder cases while families search for missing loved ones, with one student missing since October 12.
paragraphs: Vivid concern grips Bamako as disappearances and murders become almost weekly occurrences, with social media relaying search notices. While some missing individuals are found alive, others are discovered dead, leaving families distressed and searching for answers.

Habibatou Boncana Maïga, a 21-year-old student, vanished from her home on October 12, and her father reports no progress from police in locating her phone. Separately, Bocar Ly, a young man reported missing, was found dead, and another young person's body was discovered in Sébénikoro days earlier.

Authorities have arrested suspects in the murders of Broulaye Doumbia, Moctar Fofana, and Abocar Ly, with motives reportedly including homosexuality, attempted rape, and a vehicle sale dispute. Sociologist Mohamed Eglass suggests improved education and family vigilance could help prevent such tragedies.

ml.headline: AS Réal Bamako draws CAF Confederation Cup group stage opponents
ml.dek: The Malian club will face USM Alger, CS Sfaxien, and Black Bulls in group D.
paragraphs: AS Réal of Bamako learned its opponents for the 2026-2027 CAF Confederation Cup group stage after a draw on Wednesday, October 28, in Cairo, Egypt. The Scorpions were placed in Group D, where they will compete against two former competition winners and a Mozambican team. Their adversaries are USM Alger, CS Sfaxien, and the Black Bulls.

This draw marks AS Réal's return to this stage of the competition for the first time since the 2022-2023 season. They will face defending champions USM Alger, who also won in 2023, and three-time winners CS Sfaxien (2007, 2008, 2013). The Black Bulls of Mozambique complete the group. AS Réal qualified by eliminating ES Zarzis of Tunisia with a 5-3 aggregate score after a 3-1 away win and a 2-2 home draw.

The group stage matches are scheduled to take place from November 27, 2026, to January 24, 2027. AS Réal aims to finish in the top two of Group D to advance to the quarterfinals, a step up from their third-place finish in the 2022-2023 season. The club will need consistent performances in their six matches, three at home and three away, to achieve this goal.

ml.headline: Mali army and Russian corps kill over 200 livestock
ml.dek: More than 200 cattle and sheep were killed by the Malian army and Africa Corps near Diéma on October 28.
paragraphs: Malian soldiers and their Russian Africa Corps partners killed over 200 cattle and sheep on Wednesday, October 28, in Mangara, Dioumara commune, Diéma district, Nioro du Sahel region.
Habitations were also burned in the incident, the second of its kind in eight days in an area known for jihadist presence. The livestock represented the sole livelihood for local herding communities.
The jihadists of Jnim, linked to al-Qaïda, are known to operate in the region.

mr.headline: Mauritania seeks biodiversity funding in Armenia
mr.dek: Environment Minister Massouda Baham Mohamed Lagdaf met UN officials to discuss financing for conservation projects.
paragraphs: Mauritania presented its biodiversity protection efforts at the 17th Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity in Yerevan, Armenia. Minister of Environment and Sustainable Development Massouda Baham Mohamed Lagdaf highlighted national work on restoring degraded lands and preserving ecosystems.

During her visit, Minister Lagdaf discussed cooperation with Astrid Kozian, head of the UN Capital Development Fund mission. They explored funding for biodiversity projects, coastal ecosystem protection, and support for local communities' livelihoods.

The discussions also covered developing innovative financing tools, including bankable investment projects and risk-sharing. This aims to mobilize public and private resources for biodiversity preservation initiatives.

mr.headline: Somelec cuts power in Nouakchott for maintenance
mr.dek: Temporary electricity outages will affect five Nouakchott districts between October 30 and November 1, 2026.
paragraphs: The Mauritanian Electricity Company (Somelec) announced temporary power cuts in five Nouakchott districts from Friday, October 30 to Sunday, November 1, 2026. These maintenance works on electrical installations will last up to four hours daily in affected areas. The cuts are scheduled for Tevrag Zeina and Ksar on October 30, Teyarett and Dar al-Naïm on October 31, and Carrefour (Arafat) on November 1.

Somelec stated the work will occur at the main 33/15 kV central substation between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. The company apologized to customers for the inconvenience, explaining the outages are necessary for network maintenance and operational safety. These repairs aim to ensure the continued reliability of the electricity supply.

The maintenance operations are part of periodic upkeep for the electrical infrastructure. Somelec aims to guarantee the safe functioning of its network through these scheduled interventions. Customers are advised to prepare for potential disruptions during the specified dates.

mr.headline: Mauritania finds new study options for excluded medical students
mr.dek: The ministry is offering alternative countries for Mauritanian students denied specialization spots in Algeria.
paragraphs: Mauritania's Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research has found alternative study options for students who could not enroll in medical specialization programs in Algeria. The ministry will allow these students to study in other countries after limited capacity in Algeria prevented their admission. This action follows complaints from Mauritanian doctors excluded from scholarship lists for Algeria, despite completing all application steps.

Sidi Mohamed Ahmed, director of information systems at the ministry, told Sahara 24 that Algerian authorities could not register the students due to insufficient places. He stated the ministry proposed alternatives for students to complete their studies elsewhere. Some doctors, including Egyptian university graduates, were surprised not to find their names on final scholarship lists after submitting all required documents; 12 doctors were initially listed on the electronic platform but later removed.

The excluded doctors have filed appeals with the scholarship allocation department and contacted relevant ministry services without receiving a response. The director did not specify which countries were offered or the total number of students affected by these alternative solutions. It remains unclear if these arrangements cover all doctors who contested their exclusion from Algerian specialization scholarships.

mr.headline: Mauritania launches local development program consultations
mr.dek: Minister of Agriculture reviews phase two of an emergency local development plan in the Brakna region.
paragraphs: Minister of Agriculture and Food Sovereignty, Ahmed Babah Ould Aali, launched consultations for the second phase of an emergency program aimed at universal access to basic services for local development in the Brakna region. The consultations, held in Aleg, will identify development priorities based on citizen needs through a participatory approach. This initiative follows directives from President Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani to assess the first phase and address ongoing projects.

The minister reviewed the progress of the emergency program in Brakna, which includes 309 interventions across vital sectors. Water and sanitation projects show 100% completion, while electricity stands at 96%, education at 78.3%, and rural access at 72.5%. Livestock development has reached 67% completion, agriculture 57.5%, and youth and sports 42%. The next phase will focus on accelerating project completion and resolving identified issues.

The program's participatory approach, adopted in 2025, involved direct consultation with administrative authorities, elected officials, and local stakeholders to set development priorities. The minister emphasized the citizen's central role in the development process and urged local officials to ensure all districts and municipalities benefit from the planned interventions. Future efforts will concentrate on speeding up project execution and rectifying shortcomings.

mr.headline: Mauritania health ministry prepares new clinics
mr.dek: Health Minister Naha Hamdi Mouknass reviewed preparations for opening new health centers in Nouakchott.
paragraphs: Mauritania's Ministry of Health is preparing to open new health centers in Nouakchott, focusing on supply needs and team readiness. Minister Naha Hamdi Mouknass led a meeting with ministry officials, regional health directors, and representatives from the medical supply agency and digital transformation sector. The minister directed the medical supply agency to ensure all new centers are stocked, with a review of the supply system planned three months after launch.

A daily monitoring mechanism has been established, assigning a ministry official to each center to track progress and report to a supervision committee. This system aims to address any shortcomings before the centers become operational. Human resources are also being addressed, with training for new center staff set to begin on Thursday, combining theoretical and practical instruction to prepare them for their roles.

The training will equip staff with the skills needed for the new facilities. The supply system will be evaluated for effectiveness and necessary improvements. Daily reports will help identify and fix issues before the centers open.

mu.headline: Mauritius minister defends decision on cancelled exams
mu.dek: Education Minister Mahend Gungapersad responded to criticism over using assessed marks for SC and HSC exams.
paragraphs: Mauritius's School Certificate (SC) and Higher School Certificate (HSC) exams, cancelled on October 13 due to social unrest and security issues, will not be re-organized. Cambridge confirmed the use of assessed marks for grading. Education Minister Mahend Gungapersad defended this decision yesterday at an event in Phoenix, addressing criticism from former minister Leela Devi Dookun-Luchoomun.

Dookun-Luchoomun had previously called for Gungapersad's resignation on October 26, citing "poor management" and "failure of leadership." She questioned the risk assessment and the timing of informing Cambridge, arguing that assessed grades penalize students. Gungapersad dismissed these criticisms as inconsistent, recalling a similar proposal when he was in opposition in 2021.

The minister stated that the current situation should serve as a lesson. He plans to review the agreement with Cambridge to establish specific mechanisms for exceptional circumstances. This review aims to prevent similar issues in the future and ensure better preparedness for unforeseen events.

mu.headline: Mauritius PM meets NGOs after unrest
mu.dek: Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam initiated dialogue with youth and vulnerable family support groups on October 29.
paragraphs: Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam led a three-hour meeting with non-governmental organizations on Thursday, October 29, following recent national unrest. The consultation aimed to identify factors contributing to marginalization and exclusion and to address public concerns. Deputy Prime Minister Arianne Navarre-Marie, Minister of Social Integration Ashok Subron, Minister Delegate for Tourism Annabelle Savabaddy, and MP Rubna Daureeawo attended the session.

The government chose to start discussions with NGOs due to their close connection to ground realities and their ability to assess gaps in existing support systems. Topics covered included education, employment, poverty, mental health, drug addiction, domestic and sexual violence, discrimination, and the marginalization of artists. This initial meeting is the first step in a broader consultation process.

Future consultations will involve interfaith committees, government ministries, parastatal bodies, and other key national stakeholders. The government's stated goal is to create a roadmap with a clear timeline, deadlines, and identified responsibilities to ensure verifiable results and provide tangible prospects for young people.

mu.headline: Mauritius weighs lowering age for criminal responsibility
mu.dek: Government considers prosecuting 12-year-olds after recent riots, but experts cite concerns about system capacity and child welfare.
paragraphs: The Mauritian government is considering lowering the age of criminal responsibility to 12 years old, a move prompted by recent riots where minors were among those arrested. Currently, under the Children’s Act 2020, individuals under 14 cannot be prosecuted. The Cabinet discussed the proposal on October 14, deciding to establish a parliamentary Select Committee for further consultation.

Police reported that 16 minors were among the 151 people arrested during the unrest. However, legal experts note that any change would only apply to future cases due to constitutional protections against retroactive punishment. Past court rulings, including cases from 2010 and 2013, have highlighted significant delays within the Mauritian justice system, raising concerns about the impact of prolonged legal processes on young offenders.

Child-rights bodies and experts advise against lowering the age, with the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child recommending a minimum age of 14. They warn that early contact with the justice system can be detrimental to developing children. The proposed reform would also necessitate changes to the existing Children's Court system, which is designed for individuals aged 14 and above, requiring staff training and facility adjustments.

paragraphs: A court in Nampula has suspended construction work on Praça do Metical. The suspension came after civil society organisations opposed the project's location in the Jardim-Parque Popular. These groups argued that public spaces should remain accessible for residents' enjoyment.

The court's decision aims to halt work while it examines the project's compliance with urban space regulations. This review seeks to ensure the restoration of legality and the safeguarding of public interest. The construction had faced opposition shortly after the foundation stone was laid.

mz.headline: EU-trained units struggle against Mozambique insurgents
mz.dek: Insurgents conducted 154 attacks in five months across 16 districts, while specialised forces are misused.
paragraphs: Mozambique has created 11 rapid-reaction units with European Union assistance to combat insurgents in Cabo Delgado and Niassa. The EU trained soldiers, supplied equipment, and is helping regenerate units between deployments. However, insurgents continue to operate across an expanding area, with specialised forces often used in ways that undermine their training.

Brigadier-General Sérgio Estrela, commander of the EU Military Assistance Mission, stated that the FADM are hindered by excessive command centralisation, intelligence weaknesses, and shortages of equipment and money. He noted that insurgents conducted approximately 154 attacks over the previous five months, spread across about 120 locations in 16 districts. Abductions, used for ransom and recruits, rose from 29% of attacks in the first half of the year to 56% in the most recent quarter.

Estrela explained that this type of enemy requires mobile units capable of receiving intelligence, deploying quickly, striking, and withdrawing. Instead, some rapid-reaction forces have reportedly remained in static positions for months, performing garrison duties. These issues are not resolvable by further training courses.

paragraphs: Mozambique's economic growth remains insufficient to improve the population's living conditions, according to the Governor of the Bank of Mozambique, Felisberto Navalha. na.headline: Bank of Namibia raises repo rate by 25 basis points
na.dek: Annual home loan repayments increase by N$4 000 as prime lending rate hits 10.50%
paragraphs: The Bank of Namibia increased its repo rate by 25 basis points to 7.00% on 28 October 2026, raising the prime lending rate to 10.50%. This move will increase annual repayments on a typical N$1 million home loan by approximately N$4 000 since the start of the current interest rate hiking cycle. The central bank’s decision aims to protect the Namibia dollar’s peg with the South African rand and manage inflation.

Governor Ebson Uanguta announced the decision following a monetary policy review, noting it restores the traditional 25-basis-point gap between Namibia’s repo rate and South Africa’s policy rate. This helps limit capital outflows and supports currency stability. Households are already facing higher fuel and electricity costs, with petrol prices increasing by N$1.50 per litre and NamPower tariffs by 3.7% in October.

The agricultural sector faces pressure from higher borrowing costs, input prices, and drought risks. The Bank of Namibia forecasts 2.1% economic growth for 2026, but rising costs may affect spending. Analysts expect rates to remain between 10.50% and 10.75% through 2027, with potential cuts later in the year.

na.headline: Namibia construction bill faces calls for action
na.dek: The Construction Industries Federation of Namibia urges concrete steps as the long-awaited bill nears Cabinet submission.
paragraphs: The Construction Industries Federation of Namibia (CIF) is calling for concrete action on the construction industries bill, which works minister Veikko Nekundi says is nearing submission to the Cabinet’s legislation committee. CIF chief executive Bärbel Kirchner stated that the announcement renews hopes for establishing a construction council, over a decade after the bill was first presented to parliament. Kirchner noted previous unfulfilled promises warrant caution, recalling an earlier bill that reached the National Assembly in 2010.

Kirchner mentioned that the government promised a construction council by the end of the 2019/20 financial year, a commitment also stated in parliament by former prime minister Saara Kuugongelwa-Amadhila. Further legislative work followed consultations facilitated by then works deputy minister James Sankwasa, with a revised draft reaching the Cabinet in 2022. The CIF hopes this renewed momentum will lead to legislation and implementation, enabling measures like contractor registration and categorisation to match project sizes with local capacity.

The CIF believes an effective council could have supported measures like dividing large contracts into manageable lots to widen participation and strengthen local businesses. The federation also welcomed the local contractors development programme for SMEs. Kirchner highlighted skills shortages at technical, supervisory, and senior levels, arguing that skills development must extend beyond small contractors to prepare the sector for new projects and retain experienced personnel.

na.headline: Namibia seeks stronger business ties with Russia
na.dek: President Nandi-Ndaitwah called for joint ventures and technology transfer at the Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow.
paragraphs: Namibian President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah urged stronger business-to-business partnerships with Russia to boost investment and economic benefits. Speaking at the Third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow on Thursday, she called for joint ventures, technology transfer, and skills development to move beyond political ties into tangible economic outcomes.

The President stated that Namibia seeks partnerships to expand local production, promote value addition, and strengthen regional value chains, particularly in agriculture, energy, industry, and technology. She emphasized that historical solidarity should form the basis for a more dynamic partnership focused on practical results like industrialisation and local value addition.

Namibia also seeks cooperation in modern farming technologies, improved market access, and climate-resilient agriculture, including livestock development and disease control. Enhanced veterinary cooperation and capacity-building are seen as essential, alongside efforts to close Africa’s water investment gap and implement the Namib Declaration.

na.headline: Namibia Breweries partners launch N$13 million water security project
na.dek: The five-year Swakop Basin Collective Action Project aims to secure 386 million litres of water annually by 2030.
paragraphs: Namibia Breweries Limited (NBL), WWF Namibia, and the Global Water Challenge have signed a N$13 million, five-year agreement to improve water security in the Swakop River Basin. This initiative, also known as the NBL Water Balancing Project, aims to secure approximately 386 million litres of annual water benefits by 2030 through land restoration and improved management across 153 hectares.

The project brings together government, civil society, and the private sector to address water challenges and enhance climate resilience. Waldemar von Lieres, managing director of NBL, stated that the company has invested over N$35 million since 2015 in reducing its own water footprint. The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Land Reform remains committed to strengthening water security through sustainable management.

Interventions by 2030 will include managed aquifer recharge, removal of invasive alien plants, and improved water governance. This includes developing a Sub-Basin Water Allocation and Abstraction Plan. NBL is working towards reducing its water use to 2.4 litres per litre of product by 2030 under its Brew a Better Namibia strategy.

ne.headline: Türkiye seeks deeper Niger partnership
ne.dek: Ankara wants to boost cooperation in defense, health, education, energy, and mining.
paragraphs: Türkiye's ambassador to Niger, Özgür Arslan, stated on October 29, 2026, in Niamey that his country wants to strengthen cooperation with Niger. The ambassador spoke at a reception in Niamey celebrating the 103rd anniversary of the founding of the Republic of Türkiye. He highlighted that Türkiye's Africa policy, led by President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, is based on solidarity, mutual benefit, and respect for sovereignty.

Ambassador Arslan noted that ties with Niger have grown in defense, health, education, energy, mines, and professional training. He recalled high-level visits, including Niger's Prime Minister Ali Mahamane Lamine Zeine to Türkiye in 2024, and a Turkish delegation's visit to Niamey the same year. Niger's President Abdourahamane Tiani officially visited Ankara and Istanbul in June 2026.

Türkiye aims to deepen its political and economic relations with Niger through sustainable investments. The ambassador assured that Türkiye closely monitors Niger's security challenges and humanitarian needs. He stated that Türkiye intends to continue strengthening its ties with Niger, respecting national sensitivities and strategic priorities outlined in Niger's "Programme de Refondation de la République."

ne.headline: Niger launches 2027 Bac and BTS pre-registration
ne.dek: Online platforms open October 29 for students seeking state diplomas, with new subject integrations.
paragraphs: Pre-registration for the 2027 Baccalauréat and State Brevet de Technicien Supérieur (BTS) exams began on October 29, 2026, in Niamey. The official launch ceremony took place at the Francophonie site, with representatives from parent associations, teacher unions, and student organizations attending.

The OBEECS Director General, Pr Alhou Bassirou, announced that digital pre-registration platforms opened at 23:59 on October 29. Baccalauréat pre-registration runs until December 31, 2026, at 23:59 on www.officebacniger.com, while BTS pre-registration continues until February 28, 2027, at 23:59 on https://bts.obeecs.com.

Innovations for the 2027 session include the integration of Islamic studies into the A8 series with a coefficient of 2, and Physical and Sports Education (EPS) becoming a standalone subject with a coefficient of 1 for all candidates.
